title: Onboard redundancy: X8, hexa, power and signals
summary: A quadcopter with a failed motor is a falling object; a hexa and an X8 can keep flying — if the power, signals and firmware are designed for it. This module covers which failures each layout survives and why (yaw moments), how to distribute power on a heavy aircraft (buses, fuses, dual BECs, a backu
headings: What each layout survives Powering a heavy aircraft Per-arm currents on an X8 Firmware behavior on a failure Step 1. Failure table Step 2. Power diagram Step 3. Motor failure in SITL Step 4. Test stand
text: summary A quadcopter with a failed motor is a falling object; a hexa and an X8 can keep flying — if the power, signals and firmware are designed for it. This module covers which failures each layout survives and why yaw moments , how to distribute power on a heavy aircraft buses, fuses, dual BECs, a backup receiver , how to compute per-arm currents on an X8 and choose wire gauges and connectors, and how to test the behavior on a motor failure in SITL and on a test stand — before it happens in the air. theory What each layout survives - Quad : a failure of any motor means loss of yaw and roll control; a controlled crash at best. Redundancy is geometrically impossible. - Hexa 6 arms : one motor fails — the remaining five can hold altitude and roll/pitch, but yaw holds poorly the CW/CCW balance is broken : the aircraft slowly spins and lands. You need T/W ≥ 2 on the remaining motors. ArduPilot and PX4, without special settings, simply “give more throttle” to the others through the mixer — this works if there's thrust margin. - X8 coaxial octo : one motor fails — its coaxial partner and the opposite pair compensate for both thrust and moment: the most survivable layout with 8 motors on 4 arms. The price is a 10–20% efficiency loss of the coaxial pair. - Flat octo : like a hexa, but with a bigger margin; survives two failures in favorable positions. - VTOL : a lift motor failure in vertical mode — like a quad; in forward flight the lift motors aren't needed — a different failure logic. What else fails more often than a motor: the ESC overheating, breakdown , the power connector, the flight controller's BEC, the receiver, the GPS, one of two IMUs. Redundancy starts with a failure table, not with extra motors. Powering a heavy aircraft Example: an X8 on 6S, 8 × 4008 380KV, hover 7 A per motor, max 25 A: hover 56 A, peak 200 A. - Buses : a single power bus from the battery is a single point of failure. Option: two batteries in parallel through diode/ideal-diode ORing modules, or simply two parallel batteries with a fuse on each; one fails — you fly on the second. - Fuses : on each battery ANL/MIDI at 1.3 × the branch's maximum current , on the companion/payload branch, on the BEC. On the motors — no: the current is pulsed, so a fuse will either blow for nothing or fail to protect. - Dual BECs : two 5 V BECs with diode ORing for the FC and receiver a Pixhawk-class board accepts three sources: power module, USB, servo rail — with priority . One BEC fails — the aircraft lives on. - Receiver : two receivers primary CRSF + a backup on another band or one with diversity; ArduPilot: RC_OPTIONS , a backup input on another UART with RSSI /failover in PX4 RC_MAP , INAV — at the very least one receiver with diversity antennas. - GPS/compass : two GPS units with blending GPS_AUTO_SWITCH on DroneCAN, two compasses with priority. - IMU : H7 flight controllers have two or three IMUs — the EKF switches on its own EK3 has several cores . Per-arm currents on an X8 Each arm has two motors: arm current = 2 × motor current. Hover 14 A, maximum 50 A per arm. Arm wire 12–14 AWG; an XT60 arm connector ~30 A continuous, ~60 A briefly is too small for 50 A; an XT90 has margin. Central distribution board: 4 arms × 50 = 200 A peak — copper bus bars or a 200+ A PDB, XT90/AS150 from the battery, capacitors at the input of each ESC pair. Drop across a 30 cm 12 AWG arm wire at 50 A: R = 0.0172 × 0.6 / 3.31 ≈ 3.1 mΩ → 0.16 V, 7.8 W of heat at peak — acceptable; with 14 AWG it's 0.25 V and 12 W, already hot over long sessions. Firmware behavior on a failure - ArduPilot : the mixer normalizes the outputs; on saturation the priority is roll/pitch, then throttle, yaw last MOT_YAW_HEADROOM . A motor failure shows up in RCOU one channel at maximum, its neighbor at minimum and in the ESC telemetry RPM 0 . There's a thrust loss check the message “Potential Thrust Loss n ” : the mixer enables thrust boost and excludes the lost motor from yaw control; but survivability is still determined by thrust margin and geometry. - PX4 : has motor failure detection from ESC telemetry FD_ACT_EN , FD_ACT_MOT_TOUT and an action warning/land/ground . - INAV : the mixer has no special logic; a hexa/X8 with thrust margin keeps flying, yaw degrades. {{diagram:redundancy-schemes What each layout survives when one motor fails.}} practice Step 1. Failure table For your layout: failure of a motor each position , ESC, battery/connector, BEC, receiver, GPS, compass, IMU → does it survive / what's noticeable / what to do. A “countermeasure” column: redundancy, detection, failsafe. Step 2. Power diagram Draw the buses with fuses, dual BECs ORing , separate branches for the companion/payload. Per-arm currents, wire gauges, connectors, capacitors. Check the drops by calculation the widget in the “Electricity 101” module . Step 3. Motor failure in SITL ArduPilot SITL: SIM_ENGINE_FAIL — a bitmask of motors motor 1 → 1, motor 3 → 4, in the code engine_fail & 1<<i , SIM_ENGINE_MUL = 0 — a complete failure 0.5 — loss of half the thrust in Loiter on a hexa/X8 -f hexa / -f octa-quad , watch RCOU , altitude, yaw. Record: did it hold altitude, the yaw rotation rate, is a higher T/W needed. Repeat with -f quad — see the difference. Step 4. Test stand Aircraft secured, no props: disconnect one ESC signal, make sure the firmware doesn't panic and the others respond. With props — only on a safe stand with a tether and an observer, if at all. Lab: failure table, power diagram, SITL failure described. Automatic log check SITL : check_lab_log.py <log.bin --lab motorfail — the failure is visible saturated output , altitude held drop < 5 m , roll tracking p99 < 15°. diagnostics - Symptom: a hexa spins and falls after a motor failure - Possible cause: T/W on the remaining motors < 2, no yaw margin. - What to do: more thrust/less mass, MOT_YAW_HEADROOM, an X8 instead of a hexa. - Symptom: one X8 arm runs hotter - Possible cause: a wire/connector too thin for the double current. - What

title: PCB design in KiCad: from schematic to order, layout for EMC
summary: A “top”-level engineer isn't limited to what's for sale: if you need a 100 A current sensor with I²C, a power board for a specific frame, an adapter for the companion with the right connectors, you draw the board yourself. This module takes you through the full cycle in KiCad on a real example — an
headings: When to make your own board The KiCad cycle Example: an INA226 current sensor Layout for current Layout for EMC Fab capabilities Step 1. Calculation Step 2. Schematic and ERC Step 3. Layout and DRC Step 4. Output files Step 5. Testing the finished board (if built)
text: summary A “top”-level engineer isn't limited to what's for sale: if you need a 100 A current sensor with I²C, a power board for a specific frame, an adapter for the companion with the right connectors, you draw the board yourself. This module takes you through the full cycle in KiCad on a real example — an INA226 current sensor board with a shunt: calculating the shunt and the calibration register, the schematic and the ERC check, footprints, layout with current in mind trace width per IPC-2221 and electromagnetic compatibility, DRC for the fab's capabilities, output files for manufacturing, and testing the finished board on a flight controller. theory When to make your own board - The board you need doesn't exist, or doesn't fit in size, connectors or current. - Many identical vehicles: your own power and distribution board removes hand-soldered wiring — the main source of failures in the field module “Wiring” . - Educational value: layout forces you to understand where interference on the compass and gyro comes from. Don't: a flight controller from scratch as your first project — that means high-speed layout, an IMU, certified firmware; start with peripherals. The KiCad cycle 1. Schematic Schematic Editor : symbols, connections, net names, component values. ERC electrical rules check catches unconnected pins, two outputs on one net, forgotten power PWR_FLAG flags . 2. Footprints : each symbol gets a package 0603, SOT-23-6, MSOP-10, a JST-GH connector . A footprint error is the most expensive one: the board arrives and the chip doesn't fit. 3. Layout PCB Editor : board outline, layer stackup, component placement, traces, copper pours, vias. 4. DRC design rules check — the fab's rules: minimum trace width and clearance, holes, edge clearances. 5. Output : Gerber files for the layers, a drill file, a BOM bill of materials , a position file for automated assembly; a 3D view to check packages and connectors. Example: an INA226 current sensor The INA226 is a digital current and voltage monitor over I²C: it measures the drop across a shunt ±81.92 mV range, 2.5 µV step and the bus voltage up to 36 V — up to 8S , and computes current and power. - Shunt. Maximum current 100 A with an 81.92 mV range → R ≤ 0.82 mΩ; take 0.5 mΩ: 50 mV at 100 A, with margin. Power in the shunt, I²R: 5 W at 100 A, 0.8 W at 40 A continuous — a 2512 package or two shunts in parallel, wide copper pads for heat dissipation. - Resolution. A 2.5 µV step / 0.5 mΩ = 5 mA — it won't get more precise than that. The calibration register: CAL = 0.00512 / Current_LSB · R_shunt = 0.00512 / 0.005 · 0.0005 = 2048. - Support components. 100 nF at the supply pin, I²C pull-ups usually already on the flight controller — don't duplicate them without need , the address set by pins A0/A1, a TVS diode on the battery rail, an I²C connector with the Dronecode pinout JST-GH . - In the flight controller. ArduPilot: BATT_MONITOR — INA2xx type, the I²C bus and address BATT_I2C_BUS , BATT_I2C_ADDR , the maximum current and shunt resistance — via the INA2xx driver parameters for your version; to verify, compare with a clamp ammeter module “Measurements” . Layout for current - Trace width for a given current per IPC-2221: I = k·ΔT^0.44·A^0.725 outer layer k = 0.048, A is the cross-section in mil² . For 1 oz copper 35 µm and a +10 °C rise: 2 A — ~0.8 mm, 5 A — ~2.8 mm, 10 A — ~7.2 mm. Tens of amps are not carried by a trace: pours on both sides, 2 oz copper, rows of vias, wires and bus bars soldered to pads. - Kelvin connection of the shunt : the sense traces to the INA226 leave from the middle of the shunt pads as a separate pair, not from the power trace — otherwise the drop across the copper adds to the measurement. {{diagram:chart-trace-width Outer-layer trace width vs. current per IPC-2221: 1 oz and 2 oz copper at a 10 °C rise and 1 oz at 20 °C.}} Layout for EMC - Solid ground. On a 4-layer board: signal — ground — power — signal. The current returns along the ground directly under its trace; a slot in the pour under a trace is an antenna. - Keep high-current loops short. In a buck converter, the input capacitor goes right next to the switch and the diode/low-side switch: the loop with fast current is the main radiator on the board. - Sensitive circuits apart. IMU, compass, analog measurements — away from converters and power rails; a compass on a board with current is a bad idea module “Interference” . - Differential pairs CAN, USB — two traces side by side, equal length, over solid ground; the 120 Ω CAN terminator goes on the end node of the bus. - Connectors : ESD protection at external connectors, a keyed connector against reverse polarity, standard pinouts. Fab capabilities Cheap two-layer boards: trace and clearance from ~0.127–0.15 mm, holes from ~0.3 mm, 1 or 2 oz copper. Load the specific fab's rules into Board Setup before layout — DRC then checks exactly those. practice Step 1. Calculation For your vehicle: maximum and continuous current, battery voltage. Pick a shunt INA226 range, power, package , calculate the resolution and the calibration register, the width of the power traces or decide that the current runs through wires soldered to the shunt pads . Step 2. Schematic and ERC A new KiCad project. INA226, shunt, 100 nF, TVS, a power connector and an I²C connector JST-GH, 4 pins: +5 V, SCL, SDA, GND . Choose the address. ERC with no errors; explain or fix every warning. Step 3. Layout and DRC A two-layer board: the shunt's power pads on both sides with vias, a Kelvin pair to the INA226, a ground pour on the bottom, the I²C connector at the edge. Load the chosen fab's rules, DRC with no errors. Check the 3D view. Step 4. Output files Gerber and drill files, BOM, position file. Open the Gerbers in KiCad's built-in viewer Gerber Viewer and check every layer: outline, mask, silkscreen, holes. Ordering the board is optional. Step 5. summary: Blackbox Explorer и MAVExplorer показывают графики; инженеру нужны числа, которые можно сравнить до/после и положить в отчёт. Модуль — минимальный стек: Python + pandas + numpy + scipy + matplotlib; как прочитать лог Betaflight (через `blackbox_decode` в CSV) и ArduPilot (`.bin` через pymavlink), ка
headings: Стек и установка Чтение логов Спектр: почему Уэлч, а не один FFT Спектрограмма Метрики переходного процесса Джиттер петли Шаг 1. Прочитать Шаг 2. Спектр Шаг 3. Метрики Шаг 4. Пакет Проверка на синтетике до своего лога Что должно получиться и что записать
text: summary Blackbox Explorer и MAVExplorer показывают графики; инженеру нужны числа, которые можно сравнить до/после и положить в отчёт. Модуль — минимальный стек: Python + pandas + numpy + scipy + matplotlib; как прочитать лог Betaflight через blackbox_decode в CSV и ArduPilot .bin через pymavlink , как построить спектр гироскопа методом Уэлча, и как написать переиспользуемые функции метрик: overshoot, время установления, bounce-back, джиттер петли. Весь код — рабочий, с ожидаемыми числами. theory Стек и установка bash python3 -m venv ~/uav-venv && source ~/uav-venv/bin/activate pip install pandas numpy scipy matplotlib pymavlink blackbox_decode — из репозитория betaflight/blackbox-tools собирается make , превращает .BFL в CSV с одной строкой на цикл PID. Чтение логов Betaflight CSV : колонки time us , gyroADC 0..2 град/с, после фильтров — gyroADC , до — gyroUnfilt отдельное поле blackbox в 4.5, включается выбором полей; debug_mode = GYRO_SCALED пишет нефильтрованный гироскоп в debug , setpoint 0..3 , motor 0..3 , rcCommand 0..3 , axisP/I/D/F ... , eRPM ... при ESC-телеметрии. python import pandas as pd, numpy as np df = pd.read_csv "log.01.csv", skipinitialspace=True df.columns = c.strip for c in df.columns t = df "time us " .to_numpy / 1e6 fs = 1 / np.median np.diff t частота логирования, Гц 8000/4000/2000 gyro_roll = df "gyroADC 0 " .to_numpy ArduPilot .bin : python from pymavlink import mavutil m = mavutil.mavlink_connection "flight.bin" rows = while msg := m.recv_match type="ATT" is not None: rows.append msg.to_dict att = pd.DataFrame rows ; att "t" = att "TimeUS" / 1e6 Для гироскопа на высокой частоте — IMU обычно 1 кГц при LOG_BITMASK с RAW IMU или batch-сэмплы ISBH/ISBD до нескольких кГц для спектров; INS_LOG_BAT_MASK . Спектр: почему Уэлч, а не один FFT FFT всего лога — шумный и зависит от длины. Метод Уэлча режет сигнал на перекрывающиеся окна, берёт FFT каждого и усредняет: оценка спектральной плотности с контролируемым разрешением Δf = fs / nperseg . python from scipy.signal import welch f, pxx = welch gyro_roll, fs=fs, nperseg=1024, noverlap=512, window="hann" pxx_db = 10 np.log10 pxx + 1e-12 При fs = 8000 и nperseg = 1024 разрешение 7.8 Гц; пик мотора на 250 Гц виден как бугор шириной 2–3 бина. Сравнивать логи — только при одинаковых fs и nperseg. Сегмент для спектра — висение или ровный полёт 10–20 с, без газа в пол иначе пики размазываются по частотам . Спектрограмма python from scipy.signal import spectrogram f, tt, S = spectrogram gyro_roll, fs=fs, nperseg=512, noverlap=256 imshow 10 log10 S , aspect="auto", origin="lower", extent= tt 0 , tt -1 , f 0 , f -1 Показывает, как пики едут с оборотами моторы или стоят резонанс — модуль «Сигналы и спектры». Метрики переходного процесса По паре setpoint → gyro на одной оси: - Ошибка e t = setpoint − gyro. - Overshoot — насколько gyro перелетает setpoint после ступеньки, в % от величины ступеньки. - Время установления — через сколько мс gyro остаётся в ±5% или ±2% от setpoint. - Bounce-back — после резкой остановки стика setpoint → 0 gyro уходит в противоположную сторону: амплитуда отскока в % от пикового значения перед остановкой. - Задержка — лаг между setpoint и gyro по максимуму кросс-корреляции. Удобная реализация — не искать ступеньки вручную, а строить step response деконволюцией как PID Toolbox : считать импульсную характеристику системы setpoint→gyro по окнам и интегрировать. Проще для начала — отобрать участки, где d setpoint/dt большой, и мерить на них. python def step_metrics sp, gy, fs, thr=200.0 : """Find fast setpoint steps deg/s per sample threshold and measure response.""" d = np.diff sp idx = np.where np.abs d thr / fs 1000 0 res = for i in idx: seg_sp, seg_gy = sp i:i + int 0.25 fs , gy i:i + int 0.25 fs if len seg_gy < 10: continue target = seg_sp -1 ; base = sp i step = target - base if abs step < 50: continue resp = seg_gy - base / step normalised 0→1 overshoot = max 0.0, resp.max - 1.0 100 inside = np.abs resp - 1.0 < 0.05 settle = next k for k in range len inside if inside k: .all , None res.append {"t": i / fs, "step": step, "overshoot_pct": overshoot, "settle_ms": None if settle is None else 1000 settle / fs} return pd.DataFrame res Bounce-back : python def bounce_back sp, gy, fs, big=200.0 : """After setpoint returns to ~0 from a large value big deg/s , measure gyro reversal % of peak .""" out = hi = np.abs sp big for i in range 1, len sp : if hi i - 1 and not hi i : peak = sp i - 1 win = gy i:i + int 0.2 fs rev = -np.sign peak win out.append 100 max 0.0, rev.max / abs peak return np.array out Ориентиры для 5" Betaflight : overshoot 5–15% — хорошо; bounce-back < 10% — хорошо, 25% — много D или плохая механика. Джиттер петли python dt = np.diff t 1e6 мкс print dt.mean , dt.std , np.percentile dt, 99.9 Для 8 кГц среднее 125 мкс, std единицы мкс; std 10 — перегруженный процессор, пропуски — обрыв записи. {{diagram:log-analysis-pipeline Конвейер анализа лога на Python: CSV → DataFrame → общая ось времени → спектры и метрики → отчёт.}} practice Шаг 1. Прочитать Свой лог Betaflight CSV или ArduPilot .bin → DataFrame, fs посчитана, первые 5 строк и описание колонок выведены. Шаг 2. Спектр Выбрать 10 с висения, welch по трём осям, график в дБ до fs/2, пики подписаны частотами. Сохранить PNG. Шаг 3. Метрики step_metrics и bounce_back на roll: таблица шагов с overshoot и settle, медиана bounce-back. Сравнить с ориентирами. Шаг 4. Пакет Сложить функции в uavlog.py read_bf, read_ap, spectrum, step_metrics, bounce_back с docstring; второй лог прогоняется в три строки. Проверка на синтетике до своего лога Прежде чем верить спектру своего лога, проверь функцию на сигнале с известным ответом: синус 210 Гц плюс шум должен дать пик ровно там. python import numpy as np from scipy.signal import welch fs = 2000.0 8 kHz loop, blackbox 1/4 t = np.arange 0, 10, 1 / fs x = 5 np.sin 2 np.pi 210 t + np.random.default_rng 0 .normal 0, 1, t.size f, p = welch x, fs=fs, nperseg=int fs 1 s windows - 1 Hz resolution print f"peak at {f np

summary: Фильтры Betaflight и ArduPilot — это обработка сигналов, и настраивать их по интуиции — значит настраивать вслепую. text: summary Фильтры Betaflight и ArduPilot — это обработка сигналов, и настраивать их по интуиции — значит настраивать вслепую. Модуль даёт минимум теории, без которого спектр не читается: дискретизация и частота Найквиста, алиасинг почему 10-килогерцовая помеха видна как 2 кГц , что такое спектр и спектрограмма, как найти гармоники моторов и отделить их от резонанса рамы, и что делают LPF и notch одновременно в частотной затухание и во временной задержка областях. С Python-кодом и связкой с eRPM. theory Дискретизация и Найквист Гироскоп опрашивается с частотой fs Betaflight: 8 кГц на F4/F7/H7 с MPU6000/ICM42688; ArduPilot: 1–4 кГц с батч-логированием до 8 кГц . Теорема Котельникова–Найквиста: без искажений представимы частоты до fs/2 . Всё выше «заворачивается» алиасинг : сигнал частоты f fs/2 появляется на f − k·fs . Пример: fs = 8 кГц, помеха 10 кГц → видна как 2 кГц. Пример хуже: ArduPilot логирует IMU на 1 кГц при внутренних 4 кГц — гармоника мотора на 600 Гц в логе окажется на 400 Гц. Поэтому: спектры — по данным с известной fs, батч-логирование — для частот выше 500 Гц, аппаратный антиалиасинговый фильтр гироскопа у ICM42688 — настраиваемый — обязателен. Спектр: что по осям По горизонтали — частота Гц , по вертикали — мощность дБ или град²/с²/Гц . «Пик на 250 Гц, 20 дБ над шумом» — значит в 100 раз больше мощности, чем фон. Спектр Уэлча усредняет во времени — хорош для стационарного участка висение . Спектрограмма — спектр по времени: цветом мощность, по вертикали частота; видно, как пики едут с газом. Разрешение: частота против времени Спектр по N отсчётам различает частоты с шагом Δf = fs/N, а описывает отрезок длительностью N/fs. 8 кГц и N = 512: Δf ≈ 15.6 Гц за 64 мс; N = 4096: Δf ≈ 2 Гц, но за полсекунды — пик, который «ехал» с газом, размажется в полосу. Для висения берут длинные окна тонкое разрешение по частоте , для спектрограммы манёвров — короткие. Окно Ханна по умолчанию в scipy.signal.welch уменьшает «утечку» мощности сильного пика в соседние частоты; без окна вокруг гармоники мотора появляется ложная «юбка», похожая на шум. Гармоники моторов Основная частота мотора f₁ = RPM/60. Betaflight с ESC-телеметрией считает её из eRPM: RPM = eRPM / пары полюсов , у 2207 обычно 7 пар 14 магнитов → motor_poles = 14 . На спектрограмме — наклонные линии, повторяющиеся на 2f₁, 3f₁ лопасти, дисбаланс . У четырёх моторов — четыре близкие линии, которые сливаются в полосу. Проверка: взять eRPM из лога в тот же момент, посчитать f₁, сравнить с положением пика — совпадение ±5 Гц подтверждает, что это мотор. Резонанс против моторов - Пик горизонтальный на спектрограмме не зависит от газа — резонанс рамы/крепления/проводов. Лечится механикой или статическим notch. - Пик наклонный следит за eRPM — мотор. Лечится RPM-фильтром следит сам или балансировкой. - Широкая «подушка» внизу 20–80 Гц, растущая при резких движениях — пропвош и аэродинамика; не фильтруется без потери отклика, лечится D-term и механикой. Что делает фильтр — две точки зрения LPF 1-го порядка PT1 с частотой среза fc: в частотной области −3 дБ на fc, дальше −20 дБ/декаду ×10 по частоте = ×0.1 по амплитуде . Во временной — задержка : групповая задержка на низких частотах ≈ 1/ 2π·fc ; PT1 на 100 Гц задерживает полезный сигнал на ~1.6 мс. PT2/PT3 каскады режут круче −40/−60 дБ/декаду , но задерживают больше. Betaflight: gyro_lpf1_static_hz , dterm_lpf1_static_hz , динамический LPF по газу; ArduPilot: INS_GYRO_FILTER , ATC_RAT_ _FLTD/FLTE/FLTT . Notch с центром fₙ и шириной Q : глубокий провал только вокруг fₙ, малая задержка вне полосы. Узкий высокий Q — точный, но промахивается при изменении оборотов; широкий — надёжнее, но задерживает больше. RPM-notch — узкий, потому что знает частоту; динамический — ищет пик сам Betaflight dyn_notch_count/q/min_hz/max_hz ; ArduPilot гармонический notch INS_HNTCH_ с трекингом по газу, RPM или FFT . Цена любого фильтра — задержка, цена задержки — запас устойчивости модуль «Теория управления» . Цель тюнинга фильтров: минимум задержки при шуме моторов ниже уровня, который греет моторы D-term шум . Числа для ориентира 5" 6S висение: f₁ ≈ 250–350 Гц, пики 20–30 дБ над фоном до фильтров, после RPM-notch — ≤ 5 дБ. Задержка цепочки gyro LPF + D LPF у хорошего тюна 5" — 1–2 мс; у «тяжёлого» фильтра — 4–6 мс, и это уже заметно в bounce-back. {{diagram:peak-diagnosis Как опознать пик в спектре гироскопа по его поведению с газом и чем с ним бороться.}} {{diagram:chart-gyro-spectrum Модельный спектр гироскопа: внизу — движение аппарата полезный сигнал , пики гармоник моторов едут с газом , узкий пик резонанса рамы стоит на месте и шумовой пол.}} {{diagram:chart-aliasing Алиасинг при выборке 1 кГц: всё выше 500 Гц «складывается» в полосу 0–500 Гц — вибрация 700 Гц выглядит в данных как 300 Гц. Поэтому фильтр против алиасинга должен стоять до выборки, а не после.}} practice Шаг 0. Тренировка на синтетике Прежде чем доверять своему разбору лога — проверить его на сигнале, где ответ известен: python import numpy as np from scipy import signal fs = 8000; t = np.arange 0, 10, 1 / fs rpm = np.interp t, 0, 5, 10 , 12000, 21000, 12000 throttle up and down phase = 2 np.pi np.cumsum rpm / 60 / fs motor fundamental follows rpm x = 2.0 np.sin phase + 0.8 np.sin 2 phase motor 1x and 2x + 1.0 np.sin 2 np.pi 180 t frame resonance, fixed + np.random.default_rng 0 .normal 0, 0.5, t.size noise floor f, P = signal.welch x : 2 fs , fs, nperseg=2048 first 2 s: near-steady print "peaks Hz :", sorted int v for v in f signal.find_peaks 10 np.log10 P , prominence=10 0 f2, t2, S = signal.spectrogram x, fs, nperseg=512, noverlap=384 Ожидаемо: peaks Hz : 179, 218, 500 — ~180 Гц рама шаг сетки Welch ≈ 3.9 Гц , около 220 Гц мотор за 2 с обороты успели вырасти с 200 до ~260 Гц, пик размазан , около 500 Гц край размазанной второй гармоники; на спектрограмме S построить pcolormesh t2, f2, 10 log10 S , 0–1000 Гц моторные линии наклонные, линия 180 Гц горизонтальная. Если ваш код показывает иное — ошибка в коде, а не в дроне. Шаг 1. Спектрогр

text: summary Blackbox is the flight data recording system in Betaflight that captures the controller state on every control loop cycle up to 8 kHz . The log contains the gyro, accelerometer, stick signals, PID controller activity, motor outputs and filter parameters. This article gives you a complete understanding of how to set up logging, interpret the graphs and use the tools Blackbox Explorer, PIDscope for troubleshooting and tuning. After studying it, you'll be able to identify your drone's noise structure, estimate filter latency, and tune PIDs and filters based on objective data rather than random trial and error. theory Purpose and architecture of Blackbox Blackbox records the internal state of the flight controller at the highest possible rate, to enable offline simulation, debugging and analysis of control algorithms using real flight data. The log is built from frames of several types: - I-frames intra — full frames, independently decodable. - P-frames inter — delta frames, using prediction. - G/H frames — for GPS data. - S frames slow — rarely changing states. - E frames event — state transitions. Compression uses predictors and variable-length encoding, which lets you store a large amount of data at a moderate data rate. What exactly is logged Blackbox records: - time, - P/I/D values and the summed output, - setpoint sticks , - gyro and accelerometer data, - voltage/current, RSSI, - ESC commands, - GPS frames if present . Log format and storage devices Logging can go to: - onboard flash usually 2–16 MB , - an SD card preferred for long sessions , - an external logger over UART. For an SD card, FAT32 and a card with low write latency are recommended. How settings affect log quality - 1 kHz — basic PID analysis; - 2 kHz or 1.6 kHz for BMI270 — detailed noise/filter analysis. If the looptime is small high PID rate , you may need to raise the baud rate or lower the logging rate, otherwise you can get dropped frames. Physical meaning of the noise spectrum - <20 Hz — useful dynamics; - 20–100 Hz — vibration/propwash/PID problems; - 100–250 Hz — frame resonances/play; - 250 Hz — motor/prop noise and harmonics. The goal of filtering is to suppress high-frequency noise without adding extra latency in the useful range. Logging parameters blackbox_device SPIFLASH / SDCARD / SERIAL , blackbox_sample_rate 1/1, 1/2, 1/4, … of the PID rate: with 8 kHz PID and 1/4 — a 2 kHz log , blackbox_mode NORMAL — on arm; MOTOR_TEST; ALWAYS — on the ground too: for measuring gyro noise/bias , blackbox_high_resolution more precise gyro/setpoint , blackbox_disable_ disable field groups: acc , rc , gyrounfilt , rpm , gps … — saves bandwidth , debug_mode which 8 debug values to log: GYRO_SCALED — raw gyro before the filters 4.5 only; removed in 2025.12, use the gyroUnfilt field , RPM_FILTER , D_LPF , DSHOT_RPM_TELEMETRY , FEEDFORWARD , GPS_RESCUE_ , RTH … . Data rate: 2 kHz with the full set of fields is around 60–100 KB/s → 16 MB of flash is enough for 3–4 minutes; SD — hours. An external logger is the Blackbox function on a UART in the Ports tab serial <id 128 … with the blackbox baud ; there are no separate blackbox_uart / blackbox_baud settings in 4.5 and 2025.12. The fields you need most often gyroADC 0..2 after the filters , gyroUnfilt 0..2 before, if the field is enabled , setpoint 0..3 , rcCommand 0..3 , axisP/I/D/F 0..2 , motor 0..3 , eRPM 0..3 , vbatLatest , amperageLatest , rssi , debug 0..7 , flightModeFlags , stateFlags , failsafePhase ; events E-frames : arm/disarm, mode change, failsafe. The log header contains about 190 key parameters PIDs, rates, filters, motors , but not the whole diff : there's no aux , serial , OSD, failsafe — a full backup only via diff all . Reading a log in 5 minutes 1. Blackbox Explorer: overview — any gaps dropped frames , vbat under load, rssi/LQ . 2. Gyro spectrogram before/after — motors, resonances the “Signals and spectra” module . 3. Overlay setpoint on gyro for roll — overshoot/bounce-back by eye; axisD — noise. 4. motor 0..3 — symmetry one higher than the others = imbalance/mechanical issue , saturation at 100%. 5. Numbers — via Python data-python , into a decision table. Worked example: “one motor runs hotter” In the log, motor 2 at hover is 8% higher than the others and eRPM 2 is lower — the motor is producing less thrust: a damaged prop, a bearing or a twisted frame; the noise in gyroUnfilt at 2×RPM of that motor is higher. The fix is mechanical, not PID. Without a log this would have looked like “need to bump up D”. {{diagram:blackbox-chain Where in the flight controller loop the main Blackbox fields come from and how the log gets into the analysis tools.}} practice Preparing hardware and software Hardware: - an FC with flash or an SD slot, - ESCs with Bidirectional DShot BLHeli_32/Bluejay , - a high-quality, mechanically stiff build. Setup: - enable BLACKBOX , - set the logging rate usually 2 kHz , - for noise analysis use debug_mode = GYRO_SCALED , - enable the RPM filter. Recording a log and maneuvers Blackbox usually starts on arm and stops on disarm. For a good analysis, fly: - hover and straight-and-level flight, - throttle sweep 20% - 100% , - sharp rolls/flips, - throttle pumps, - sharp turns propwash check . Working with Blackbox Explorer 1. Download the .bbl Mass Storage Mode . 2. Open the log in Blackbox Explorer. 3. Check the header i — it has all the firmware parameters. 4. For analysis, select Gyro , Setpoint , P/I/D , Motor , Debug . 5. Use I/O to select sections of equal length. PIDscope formerly PIDtoolbox Since 2024 PIDtoolbox has been distributed as a paid subscription product; its open continuation is PIDscope GPL-3.0, runs in the free GNU Octave, supports Betaflight 4.x and 2025.12 logs . It's useful for: - estimating filter latency, - comparing spectra in dB, - step response analysis. Step-by-step filter tuning 1. Record a log with GYRO_SCALED and a throttle sweep . 2. Assess the spectrum: - <100 Hz is usually solved with mechanics/PID,

Preparation Step 1. Baseline Step 2. Reading the spectrum Step 3. Decisions from the table Step 4. Locking it in Lab Automatic log check
text: summary Filters sit between the gyro and the PID controller and decide what the controller “sees”: the useful movement of the frame, or motor noise, resonances and vibration on top of it. Without them the D-term turns noise into motor jitter and heat; with too much, every filter adds delay, the aircraft becomes “mushy” and the stability margin melts away. This module walks through the Betaflight 4.5 filter chain in the order the code applies it LPF2 when downsampling → RPM notch → static notches → LPF1 → dynamic notch for the gyro; notch → LPF1 → LPF2 for the D-term , explains each parameter with its default values, gives a method for tuning from the Blackbox spectrum with concrete “good enough” criteria, and shows where filters do not help mechanics, propwash . The interactive part: the chain's frequency response and group delay. theory What exactly we filter and why The gyro signal = frame movement 0–100 Hz, useful + noise. Noise sources and where they sit in the spectrum more in the “Frame and vibration” and “Signals and spectra” modules : {{diagram:fc-signal-path Where the filters sit in the chain: between the gyro and the PID; whatever they let through ends up in the D-term and on the motors.}} Source Frequency on a 5" 6S Look on the spectrogram Cure --- --- --- --- Motor fundamental imbalance 250–450 Hz at hover, up to 700+ at throttle a slanted line that follows throttle RPM filter 2nd, 3rd harmonics blades, aerodynamics ×2, ×3 parallel lines RPM filter harmonics Frame / FC mount resonance 100–300 Hz a horizontal line mechanics, dynamic notch, static notch Broadband noise play, bad bearings, electrical the whole range a “cushion” mechanics, LPF Propwash 20–80 Hz bursts during sharp moves not filters: D-term, mechanics, props The main victim of noise is the D-term : the derivative amplifies the signal in proportion to frequency 40 times more at 400 Hz than at 10 Hz , so the motors “hum” and heat up, while P and I barely notice the noise. Hence two chains: a gentle one for the gyro it feeds all three terms and a harsher one for D. Filter types and the price of each - PT1 — a first-order filter: −3 dB at the cutoff frequency fc, then −20 dB/decade; group delay at low frequencies ≈ 1/ 2π·fc PT1 100 Hz → 1.6 ms; 250 Hz → 0.64 ms . The “cheapest” in delay. - PT2, PT3 — cascades of PT1: −40/−60 dB/decade, delay ×1.6/×2.2 relative to a PT1 with the same fc. Used when you need to cut noise above the band sharply at moderate delay the D-term LPF defaults to PT1 in 4.5; the type is changed with _lpf1_type / _lpf2_type : PT1, BIQUAD, PT2, PT3 . - BIQUAD 2nd order, Butterworth — steeper than PT1, delay between PT1 and PT2. - Notch — a dip around the center frequency with a width set by Q the higher Q, the narrower ; outside the band the delay is almost zero. That's why narrowband motor noise is properly cut with notches rather than by lowering the LPF. The price of filtering is delay; the price of delay is phase margin the “Control theory” module : with a total gyro+D chain delay of about 1–2 ms, a good 5" tune holds P/D 30–50% higher than with 4–6 ms. {{widget:filter-response}} The gyro chain in Betaflight 4.5 parameters; the actual order in filterGyro : LPF2 → RPM → static notches → LPF1 → dynamic notch 1. RPM filter rpm_filter_harmonics = 3 , rpm_filter_q = 500 , rpm_filter_min_hz = 100 , rpm_filter_fade_range_hz = 50 , rpm_filter_lpf_hz = 150 , rpm_filter_weights = 100,100,100 — one notch per harmonic per motor 3 harmonics × 4 motors = 12 notches , with the center taken from eRPM via bidirectional DShot dshot_bidir = ON , motor_poles = 14 for a 2207/2306 with 14 magnets . Q = 500 means a width of ≈ f/5: narrow and precise. min_hz — below this frequency no notch is placed so the useful signal isn't cut at low throttle , fade_range_hz — a smooth fade-in above min_hz. There's a separate module, “RPM filter”. 2. Dynamic notch dyn_notch_count = 3 , dyn_notch_q = 300 , dyn_notch_min_hz = 100 , dyn_notch_max_hz = 600 : an FFT on the gyro finds the strongest peaks in the min..max range and puts notches on them. It catches what the RPM filter doesn't know about — frame resonances. With the RPM filter, count = 1–2 and q = 300–500 is enough; without the RPM filter — count = 4–5 , q = 250–300 wider . 3. LPF1 — dynamic by default: the cutoff slides with throttle from gyro_lpf1_dyn_min_hz = 250 to gyro_lpf1_dyn_max_hz = 500 gyro_lpf1_dyn_expo sets the curve ; with gyro_lpf1_static_hz ≠ 0 and dyn_min = 0 — static. Type gyro_lpf1_type = PT1 . 4. LPF2 — static gyro_lpf2_static_hz = 500 , PT1: a safety anti-aliasing cutoff. Static notches gyro_notch1_hz/cutoff , gyro_notch2_hz/cutoff 0 = off — for one known resonance you don't want to hand to the dynamic notch. Plus the gyro's hardware filter in the chip gyro_hardware_lpf = NORMAL — on an ICM42688 this is the DLPF, and it already sits in the signal path before all the software filters. The D-term chain dterm_lpf1_ — dynamic by default dterm_lpf1_dyn_min_hz = 75 , dterm_lpf1_dyn_max_hz = 150 , dterm_lpf1_type = PT1 , dterm_notch_hz/cutoff 0 = off , dterm_lpf2_static_hz = 150 PT1 . Two to three times lower than the gyro ones, because D amplifies high frequencies. It's the D filters that contribute most of the chain's delay and are the first to “blur” the response. Sliders and when they're enough simplified_gyro_filter = ON , simplified_gyro_filter_multiplier = 100 and simplified_dterm_filter_multiplier = 100 scale all the cutoff frequencies at once: 100 = defaults, 150 = 50% higher less filtering, less delay , 50 = half. For a clean 5" with the RPM filter, the practice is: gyro 100–150, D-term 100–130. The slider is the first tool; manual parameters are for when the spectrum shows a specific problem. “Filtered enough” criteria From the post-filter spectrum a log with debug_mode = GYRO_SCALED gives before/after : motor peaks ≤ 5–10 dB above the floor; no peaks above 10 dB in the 100–300 Hz band resonances ; D-term debug_mode = D_LPF or axisD in the log without

text: summary An ESC is a separate computer with its own firmware, and that firmware decides the RPM filter, how the motors sound, how hot they run and even whether a motor will start after a crash. The “Motors and ESC” module explained what an ESC does; here you'll learn which firmware goes on which hardware, what bidirectional DShot and EDT are, which ESC settings actually change how it flies PWM frequency, timing, demagnetization, startup power , how to flash through the flight controller in Betaflight and ArduPilot, and how not to turn a 4-in-1 into a brick. theory Who's who Firmware Hardware Status What matters --- --- --- --- BLHeli_S 8-bit EFM8 BB1/BB2/BB21 factory firmware on cheap ESCs, no longer developed no bidirectional DShot in its original form Bluejay 8-bit EFM8 BB21 and BB51 BB1/BB10 only up to version 0.18.1 open source, actively developed bidirectional DShot, EDT, PWM frequency 24/48/96 kHz, startup melodies BLHeli_32 32-bit ARM closed source; development and support ended in 2024 it works, but there will be no updates or new configurator AM32 32-bit ARM STM32F051, G071, AT32F421, GD32, etc. open source, actively developed a replacement for BLHeli_32 where a target exists for the board The firmware name on the box tells you about the ESC's microcontroller: “BLHeli_S” means 8-bit, “BLHeli_32” or “AM32” means ARM. Bidirectional DShot and EDT - DShot is a digital command protocol from the flight controller to the ESC: DShot300/600 is the speed in kbit/s; no throttle range calibration, with a checksum. - Bidirectional DShot bidir : over the same wire, the ESC replies with electrical RPM eRPM . This is the input for the Betaflight RPM filter and the harmonic notch in ArduPilot. Mechanical RPM = eRPM / number of poles / 2 , so the motor's pole count usually 14 for 22xx–28xx must be set in the flight controller. - EDT Extended DShot Telemetry adds the ESC's temperature, voltage, current and status to the same replies, with no separate telemetry wire. Supported by Bluejay and AM32; you enable it in the flight controller. Settings that change how it flies - PWM frequency. Higher 48–96 kHz is quieter and smoother at low throttle, with better response; lower 24 kHz means less switching loss and heat, and more “thrust per amp” on heavy aircraft. For 5" freestyle 48 kHz is typical, for big props 24. - Timing advance . The commutation advance angle. Higher means more RPM and current, and heat; lower is more efficient, but risks losing sync on sharp throttle changes. Auto/medium is a sensible start. - Demagnetization demag compensation . Protection against losing sync on sharp throttle changes with big motors. Desyncs the motor twitches or stops in flight are treated first by raising the compensation. - Startup power startup/rampup power . Too high and the windings burn when the motor is jammed; too low and a heavy motor won't start. - Rotation direction. Changed in the ESC firmware or with a DShot command from the flight controller; no need to resolder wires. - Melodies and beacon. The “lost drone” sound after a crash is a useful feature, not a toy. How to flash - Through the flight controller passthrough . The flight controller routes the ESC signal wire through to the computer. Betaflight: connect USB, close the Configurator the port is busy , open ESC Configurator esc-configurator.com in Chrome for BLHeli_S/Bluejay and AM32; for BLHeli_32 use BLHeliSuite32 the archived version . ArduPilot: SERVO_BLH_AUTO = 1 for the motors on planes, SERVO_BLH_MASK , DShot protocol, disconnect the GCS, keep USB, and in the configurator choose the “BLHeli32/AM32 Bootloader Betaflight/Cleanflight ” interface. IOMCU outputs MAIN don't support passthrough; you need the FMU/AUX outputs. - The target rule. The firmware is chosen for the specific ESC board layout/target . A wrong target ranges from misbehavior to burned MOSFETs. The configurator usually shows the current layout; flash only a matching one. - Before flashing : remove the props, save the current settings a screenshot or a file , flash one ESC at a time if in doubt, use a protected battery smoke stopper . Flight controller: what to enable - Betaflight: set motor_pwm_protocol = DSHOT600 or 300 , set dshot_bidir = ON , set motor_poles = 14 ; to check, the Motors tab shows RPM, DShot errors ≈ 0%. - ArduPilot: MOT_PWM_TYPE set to DShot300/600, SERVO_BLH_BDMASK is the mask of outputs with bidirectional DShot, SERVO_BLH_POLES is the pole count; ESC telemetry shows up in the log ESC and is used by the harmonic notch INS_HNTCH_MODE = 3 , driven by ESC telemetry . {{diagram:esc-firmware-choice Choosing ESC firmware: an 8-bit ESC on BB21/BB51 gets Bluejay instead of BLHeli_S, a 32-bit one gets AM32 if a target exists, a working BLHeli_32 can stay, and without a target don't flash.}} practice Step 1. Inventory Read each ESC through passthrough: firmware and version, layout/target, PWM frequency, timing, direction. Write the table into the aircraft's passport. Step 2. Bidir DShot and RPM If the firmware supports it, enable bidirectional DShot and the pole count in the flight controller. Betaflight: the Motors tab, with the motors spinning no props , shows RPM and the error percentage. Write down eRPM and mechanical RPM at 10% throttle and check the conversion formula with your pole count. Step 3. Flashing if there's a benefit Only if you need bidir DShot or EDT that you don't have: BLHeli_S → Bluejay only on BB21/BB51 MCUs or BLHeli_32 → AM32 if a target exists. Save the settings first; take the target from the layout you read. After flashing, restore the direction and check the motor order and direction. Step 4. PWM frequency on the bench Don't measure without props: you need a real operating mode. With props, tethered or in flight: two flights with the same pack at 24 and 48 kHz Bluejay/AM32 . Compare in Blackbox or the log: hover current, ESC temperature EDT , gyro noise. Write down the conclusion for your aircraft. The lab counts as done when the ESC tabl

text: summary A breakdown of a real case: a 10-inch quadcopter's motors “whistle” and it flies unevenly. The cause turned out to be not the PID but a single line of config: the lower bound of the RPM filter was above the motors' rotation frequency, and for most of the flight the filter simply wasn't working. This module teaches you to check whether the RPM filter covers the real RPM range using Blackbox data, not by eye. theory How the RPM filter works With bidirectional DShot, each ESC reports its motor's eRPM to the flight controller. Betaflight converts eRPM into RPM using motor_poles and places narrow notch filters exactly on each motor's rotation frequency and its harmonics. By default that's 12 notch filters per axis 4 motors × 3 harmonics on roll, pitch and yaw. The notch “tracks” the RPM in real time, so it cuts motor noise with almost no extra delay. Why big props have different math The frequency of a motor's fundamental harmonic: f = RPM / 60 . A five-inch in hover spins at tens of thousands of RPM, and the fundamental sits in the hundreds of hertz. A 10-inch has low-speed motors low KV, heavy props , and the fundamental in hover can drop to 50–100 Hz. The rpm_filter_min_hz parameter sets the lower bound: the notch doesn't go below it. If the bound is above the motor's real frequency, the filter sits “off target” from the noise. That's exactly what happened in the case below. Hardware requirements - An ESC with DShot telemetry support: BLHeli_32 from 32.7.0, AM32, Bluejay BLHeli_S or JESC. - dshot_bidir = ON and a correct motor_poles the number of magnets in the bell, not the number of stator teeth . - Telemetry errors in the Motors tab no higher than 1%. If an ESC doesn't report valid telemetry, Betaflight blocks arming with the DSHOT_TELEM flag in the OSD/ status . Case: viking10, iFlight Blitz F722, 10" The pilot's complaint: the motors whistle, the flight is uneven. A spectrum analysis of the log Python, orangebox + scipy showed: - motor fundamental: p5 = 48 Hz, median 91 Hz, p95 = 165 Hz; - the config had rpm_filter_min_hz = 100 — meaning for more than half the flight the motor spun below the bound and the RPM filter didn't see it; - in the 80–150 Hz band the filtered gyro was only ~2 dB quieter than raw, D-term +44.5 dB — that's the “whistle”; - static notches sat at 68 Hz, while the motors in hover ran at 84–96 Hz — the filters were cutting empty air. The fix: rpm_filter_min_hz = 50 , static notches removed, gyro LPF returned to default. After the next flight, in the same 80–150 Hz band: filtered gyro −9.5 dB was +24.4 , D-term −1.0 dB was +44.5 , motor command noise dropped from ~450 to ~20 arbitrary units. eRPM errors — 0%. The takeaway: before touching the PID, check that the filters sit where the noise actually lives. Parameters 4.5 and what they mean Parameter Default Meaning --- --- --- dshot_bidir OFF → ON eRPM telemetry over the same DShot line motor_poles 14 number of magnets; eRPM/ poles/2 = RPM rpm_filter_harmonics 3 harmonics 1×, 2×, 3× of the motor frequency rpm_filter_weights 100,100,100 “weight” depth of each harmonic in %; the 2nd and 3rd can often be weakened to 50–80 on clean aircraft → less delay rpm_filter_q 500 Q factor: notch width ≈ f/ Q/100 ; 500 → f/5 rpm_filter_min_hz 100 below it no notch is placed protects the useful band ; for 10" — 50 rpm_filter_fade_range_hz 50 smooth fade-in of the notch above min_hz rpm_filter_lpf_hz 150 filter on the eRPM estimate itself smoothing telemetry jumps The effect can only be measured with the spectrum: before/after attenuation of 20–30 dB in the harmonic band is normal; less than 10 dB — something is wrong polarity/poles/E% . Why the RPM filter lets you raise D D noise ∝ frequency × gyro noise amplitude. Once the narrow motor peaks are removed, you can raise the D-LPF frequencies less delay and D more damping at the same motor temperature — that's what gave the jump in flight quality in 4.1+, not “new PIDs.” Worked example: a 7" with Bluejay BLHeli_S ESC → flash Bluejay 48 kHz , dshot_bidir = ON , motor_poles = 14 2806.5 , Motors tab: RPM on all four, E = 0%; rpm_filter_min_hz = 70 hover ~110–130 Hz on a 7" , rpm_filter_harmonics = 3 , weights 100/80/60; spectrum: 125 Hz peak −27 dB; dyn_notch_count 1 for the frame; after that — simplified_gyro_filter_multiplier 120, D-term 110; bounce-back 14 → 9%, motors warm. {{diagram:rpm-filter-chain RPM filter: eRPM from the ESC is converted into the motor frequency and its harmonics, a notch is placed on each; rpm_filter_min_hz limits it from below.}} {{diagram:chart-rpm-harmonics Why the viking10 case broke: the motor fundamental was 48–165 Hz median 91 Hz, hover 84–96 Hz, i.e. ~5000–5800 RPM , and the 100 Hz lower bound kept the notch above the noise for more than half the flight. A 50 Hz bound puts the filter back on the harmonic.}} {{widget:rpm-harmonics}} practice Step 1. Enable and check telemetry Connect the battery without it the Motors tab will show E: 100% and run in the CLI: set dshot_bidir = ON set motor_poles = 14 save After the reboot, always read the values back. Betaflight can silently correct an incompatible combination for example, the DShot protocol on a particular board : get dshot_bidir get motor_pwm_protocol status The dshot_telemetry_info command should show telemetry for all motors with near-zero errors status doesn't print it . Step 2. Find the real range of motor frequencies 1. Enable Blackbox with a logging rate of at least 1 kHz and do a normal flight with hovering. 2. In Blackbox Explorer or PID Toolbox look at the eRPM field or the gyro spectrum and find the minimum frequency in hover and on throttle cuts. 3. The raw eRPM n field blackbox_decode/orangebox is stored in units of 100 eRPM: Hz = eRPM × 100 / motor_poles / 2 / 60 ; Blackbox Explorer shows rpm and Hz on its own. Step 3. Adjust the lower bound Set rpm_filter_min_hz below the motor's minimum operating frequency, with margin: get rpm_filter set rpm_filter_min_hz = 50 save For a 5" the de

Модуль объясняет на уровне, достаточном для инженера: что такое устойчивость замкнутого контура, почему задержка съедает запас по фазе и приводит к осцилляциям при большом P, как step response связан с полюсами и демпфированием (и почему bounce-back — это недодемпфир
headings: Объект, регулятор, контур Модель оси в первом приближении Устойчивость и запас по фазе Step response, полюса, демпфирование I-term: статическая ошибка и windup Feedforward Каскад: угол → скорость Что это значит для тюнинга Шаг 1. Симулятор: предел P при двух задержках Шаг 2. ζ по overshoot Шаг 3. Bounce-back ↔ D Шаг 4. Каскад Числа для самопроверки Что должно получиться и что записать
text: summary PID-тюнинг без теории — перебор. Модуль объясняет на уровне, достаточном для инженера: что такое устойчивость замкнутого контура, почему задержка съедает запас по фазе и приводит к осцилляциям при большом P, как step response связан с полюсами и демпфированием и почему bounce-back — это недодемпфированный полюс , и почему автопилот строит каскад угол → угловая скорость с внутренним контуром в разы быстрее внешнего. Формулы минимальны, каждая привязана к тому, что видно в симуляторе PID и в логе. theory Объект, регулятор, контур Объект — аппарат: вход — команда моторам, выход — угловая скорость. Регулятор — PID: вход — ошибка setpoint − gyro , выход — команда. Замкнутый контур: выход влияет на вход через измерение. Весь смысл теории — предсказать поведение контура, не замыкая его. Модель оси в первом приближении Момент двигателей создаёт угловое ускорение: J·ω̇ = M − b·ω, где J — момент инерции, b — аэродинамическое демпфирование. Передаточная функция от момента к ω — апериодическое звено 1/ J·s + b — «интегратор с утечкой»: ω растёт, пока прикладывается момент. Плюс запаздывания : мотор ток/обороты, τ ≈ 10–30 мс для 5" , фильтры гироскопа и D 1–5 мс , период петли и ESC-протокола 0.1–0.5 мс . Суммарная чистая задержка T_d — главный враг. Устойчивость и запас по фазе Контур с P-регулятором: при малом P — вялый, при большом — осцилляции, при ещё большем — расходящиеся. Граница — там, где петлевое усиление на частоте, на которой фазовый сдвиг достигает −180°, равно 1. Чистая задержка T_d даёт фазовый сдвиг −360°·f·T_d: на 50 Гц при T_d = 5 мс это −90°, и полюс объекта добавляет ещё −90° — вот и −180°. Поэтому: - Запас по фазе — сколько градусов до −180° на частоте, где усиление = 1. 45–60° — хороший тюн небольшой overshoot ; 20–30° — звон и bounce-back; 0 — незатухающие осцилляции. - Задержка T_d съедает запас линейно с частотой: чем быстрее хочешь контур выше P , тем больше теряешь. Удвоение задержки при том же P — потеря ~половины запаса. - Отсюда ограничение «P не больше, чем позволяет задержка». Снижение задержки фильтры повыше, RPM-notch вместо широкого LPF, быстрый ESC-протокол, лёгкие пропы — единственный способ поднять P без осцилляций. Step response, полюса, демпфирование Замкнутый контур второго порядка описывается собственной частотой ωₙ и демпфированием ζ: - ζ 1 — апериодический, медленный; - ζ ≈ 0.7 — быстрый с overshoot ~5%; это цель; - ζ = 0.4 — overshoot ~25%, звон; - ζ → 0 — осцилляции. Overshoot ≈ exp −π·ζ/√ 1−ζ² : 0.7 → 4.6%, 0.5 → 16%, 0.3 → 37%. Время установления ≈ 4/ ζ·ωₙ . Bounce-back после остановки стика — тот же недодемпфированный полюс, только возбуждённый ступенькой «вниз»: большой bounce-back = низкое ζ = либо мало D, либо много P/задержки. D-term повышает демпфирование ζ — поэтому «много D» убирает отскок, но D усиливает шум ∝ частоте, и фильтры D добавляют задержку, которая снова снижает запас. Это и есть компромисс тюнинга. I-term: статическая ошибка и windup I убирает установившуюся ошибку ветер, несимметрия . Платит фазой: интегратор даёт −90° на низких частотах, поэтому слишком большой I — медленные колебания 0.5–3 Гц, «плавание» . Windup — накопление I при насыщении выходов стик в упоре, моторы в потолке : прошивки ограничивают iterm_limit , iterm_relax , в ArduPilot ATC_RAT_ _IMAX . Feedforward FF подаёт команду пропорционально производной setpoint, минуя ошибку: выход начинает двигаться до того, как накопилась ошибка. Не влияет на устойчивость вне контура , но даёт overshoot при резких стиках, если его много. Хороший FF — малая задержка отклика при том же P. Каскад: угол → скорость Внешний контур angle считает желаемую угловую скорость из ошибки угла; внутренний rate отрабатывает её. Правило: внутренний контур должен быть в 3–10 раз быстрее внешнего полоса , иначе внешний «видит» динамику внутреннего и каскад осциллирует. В ArduPilot: ATC_ANG_RLL_P внешний, ~4.5–12 и ATC_RAT_RLL_P/I/D внутренний ; поверх — контур позиции PSC_ ещё медленнее. В Betaflight angle mode: angle_p_gain 4.5 поверх rate PID. В PX4: MC_ROLL_P → MC_ROLLRATE_P/I/D . Автотюн настраивает сначала внутренний контур, потом внешний — по той же причине. Что это значит для тюнинга 1. Сначала снизить задержку механика, фильтры , потом поднимать P. 2. P — до начала звона, потом назад на 20–30% запас по фазе . 3. D — пока bounce-back не станет < 10% и моторы не греются. 4. I — до исчезновения дрейфа, без «плавания». 5. Внешний контур — после внутреннего. Откуда берётся суммарная задержка T_d и какое звено весит больше всего — посчитай для своей связки: {{widget:link-latency}} {{diagram:angle-rate-cascade Каскад «угол → угловая скорость»: внешний P по углу задаёт уставку внутреннему PID по гироскопу.}} {{diagram:chart-step-responses Переходный процесс системы второго порядка: ζ = 0.7 даёт ~5 % перерегулирования и быстрое установление — цель для контура угловой скорости; ζ = 0.3 звенит, ζ = 1 вялый.}} practice Шаг 1. Симулятор: предел P при двух задержках В интерактивном симуляторе PID модуль «PID-регулятор в Betaflight» : задержка 2 мс — поднимать P до начала незатухающих осцилляций, записать P_max и частоту; задержка 5 мс — повторить. Ожидаемо: P_max заметно ниже, частота осцилляций ниже. Шаг 2. ζ по overshoot По логу data-python → step_metrics : overshoot → ζ по формуле; время установления → ωₙ. Сравнить две оси. Шаг 3. Bounce-back ↔ D Взять лог до/после изменения D на 20%: медиана bounce-back и шум моторов. Объяснить через ζ и задержку. Шаг 4. Каскад ArduPilot SITL: ATC_ANG_RLL_P поднять с 4.5 до 15 при стандартном rate-тюне — наблюдать осцилляции по углу; объяснить соотношением полос. Числа для самопроверки - ζ по перелёту второй порядок : ζ = −ln OS / √ π² + ln² OS . Перелёт 10 % → ζ ≈ 0.59; 25 % → ζ ≈ 0.40. Ниже 0.4 отклик звенит, выше 0.8 — вялый. - ωₙ по времени установления 2 % : t_s ≈ 4 / ζ·ωₙ . Пример: t_s = 40 мс при ζ = 0.6 → ωₙ ≈ 4 / 0.6 · 0.04 ≈ 167 рад/с ≈ 27 Гц. - Задержка против предела P шаг 1 : с ростом задержки допустимый P падает, а частота незатухающих колебаний

title: System identification: chirp, frequency response, a model for tuning
summary: Тюнинг «на глаз» и даже AUTOTUNE отвечают на вопрос «какие коэффициенты», но не «почему». Идентификация системы отвечает: аппарату подают известный сигнал (чирп — синусоиду с растущей частотой), записывают реакцию, считают частотную характеристику и подгоняют под неё модель с понятными параметрами —

text: summary Тюнинг «на глаз» и даже AUTOTUNE отвечают на вопрос «какие коэффициенты», но не «почему». Идентификация системы отвечает: аппарату подают известный сигнал чирп — синусоиду с растущей частотой , записывают реакцию, считают частотную характеристику и подгоняют под неё модель с понятными параметрами — постоянной времени моторов, задержкой, коэффициентом усиления. С моделью тюнинг становится расчётом: запас по фазе, частота среза, что даст фильтр. Модуль разбирает чирп и требования к эксперименту, режим SYSID в ArduCopter, оценку частотной характеристики по спектрам, подгонку модели первого порядка с задержкой и использование модели для выбора коэффициентов. Код проверяется на синтетических данных, затем — на логе SITL. theory Зачем модель - Регулятор настраивают под объект. Объект рейт-контура коптера — «команда момента → угловая скорость»: инерция корпуса, постоянная времени моторов разгон винта , задержки фильтры, ESC, расчётный цикл . - Модель вида G s = K·e^ −sτ / Ts + 1 или с интегратором — для перехода к углу описывает эту цепочку тремя числами. Зная их, можно посчитать запас по фазе для любых коэффициентов, увидеть, сколько фазы «съест» новый фильтр, и сравнить два аппарата объективно. - Модуль «Теория управления» дал язык передаточные функции, запасы ; здесь — как получить модель из полёта. Чирп и требования к эксперименту - Чирп — синусоида, частота которой растёт от f₀ до f₁ за время записи. Экспоненциальный логарифмический чирп тратит одинаковое время на каждую октаву — удобно для логарифмической оси частот. - Диапазон частот : от ниже ожидаемой полосы контура 1–2 Гц до выше частоты среза 30–60 Гц для небольших коптеров , но ниже частот, где шум и резонансы рамы. - Амплитуда : достаточно большая, чтобы сигнал был выше шума, и достаточно малая, чтобы не выйти в насыщение моторов и нелинейность. Признак насыщения — моторы на пределе в логе. - Длительность : десятки секунд — больше периодов на низких частотах, точнее оценка. - Замкнутый контур. Аппарат летит с работающими регуляторами, поэтому вход и выход связаны через регулятор. Важно, куда вводится сигнал и что берётся «входом»: оценивают отношение выхода к реальному сигналу на входе объекта например, к выходу регулятора/миксера , а не к заданию. Режим SYSID в ArduCopter - Режим «как STABILIZE», который подмешивает чирп в выбранную точку контура и пишет данные в лог сообщения SIDD — данные во времени, SIDS — настройки . - SID_AXIS — куда подмешивать угол, рейт или миксер по крену/тангажу/рысканию и др.; значения — по списку своей версии . Пока SID_AXIS = 0 , войти в режим нельзя; кроме того, аппарат должен быть в воздухе, а переключаться в SYSID для осей 1–13 можно только из режима с ручным газом STABILIZE, ACRO , для осей 14–19 — только из LOITER. - SID_MAGNITUDE — амплитуда, SID_F_START_HZ и SID_F_STOP_HZ — диапазон, SID_T_REC — длительность записи, SID_T_FADE_IN / SID_T_FADE_OUT — плавное нарастание и спад амплитуды. - Безопасность: высота, свободное пространство, пилот готов перехватить управление переключением режима; начинать с малой амплитуды, сначала в SITL. - Betaflight и PX4: в Betaflight с 2025.12 есть режим CHIRP опция сборки USE_CHIRP , параметры chirp_ , настройки пишутся в заголовок Blackbox ; в 4.5 штатного чирпа нет анализ — по Blackbox при ручных возмущениях ; в PX4 автотюн коптера сам идентифицирует модель онлайн, а для ручной идентификации есть сигнал-генераторы в тестовых сборках — по документации своей версии. Частотная характеристика по спектрам Для линейной системы Y f = H f ·U f . Оценка H = Y·U / U ², усреднённая по полосам частот: перекрёстный спектр делить на спектр входа. Усреднение по полосе подавляет шум; там, где во входе мало энергии за пределами чирпа , оценка бессмысленна. - Когерентность качество оценки — насколько выход объясняется входом линейно: близко к 1 — хорошо; падает — шум, нелинейность, другой вход ветер, пилот . - Результат — точки на диаграмме Боде: усиление в дБ и фаза в градусах. Подгонка модели Модель G s = K·e^ −sτ / Ts + 1 : - на низких частотах усиление ≈ K; - на частоте излома 1/ 2πT усиление −3 дБ, фаза −45° без задержки ; - задержка τ не меняет усиление, но добавляет −360°·f·τ фазы, растущей с частотой. Поэтому T видно по усилению, τ — по «лишней» фазе на высоких частотах. Подгонка — минимизация разницы комплексных H и G по точкам перебор по сетке T и τ, K — аналитически . На примере модуля T = 20 мс, τ = 10 мс, шум на выходе подгонка возвращает T = 20 мс и τ ≈ 9 мс: модель непрерывная, а данные — дискретные с шагом 2.5 мс, полшага задержки «теряется». {{diagram:chart-sysid-bode Частотная характеристика по чирпу: точки, посчитанные по спектрам, и модель первого порядка с задержкой; излом усиления на 8 Гц, фаза уходит вниз из-за задержки.}} Модель → тюнинг - Запас по фазе. Для пропорционального регулятора Kp разомкнутый контур L = Kp·G. Частота среза — где L = 1; запас по фазе — 180° + ∠L на ней. Чем больше Kp, тем выше частота среза и тем меньше запаса из-за задержки. - Цена фильтра. Фильтр нижних частот с частотой f_c добавляет примерно −arctan f/f_c фазы: на частоте среза контура 20 Гц фильтр 80 Гц отнимает ~14°. Это и есть «фильтры съедают запас» из модуля «Фильтры» — теперь числом. - Сравнение аппаратов и изменений. Новые винты, моторы, рама — новая модель: видно, изменилась ли постоянная времени или задержка, и сколько коэффициентов это стоит. practice Шаг 1. Синтетическая проверка Код идентификации и подгонки; сначала — на данных с известным ответом: python import numpy as np def identify u, y, fs, f_lo=1.0, f_hi=40.0, nbins=30 : """Frequency response y/u in log-spaced bins cross-spectrum / auto-spectrum .""" U, Y = np.fft.rfft u , np.fft.rfft y f = np.fft.rfftfreq len u , 1 / fs edges = np.geomspace f_lo, f_hi, nbins + 1 out = for lo, hi in zip edges :-1 , edges 1: : k = f = lo & f < hi if k.any : H = np.sum Y k np.conj U k / np.sum np.abs U k 2 out.append np.sqrt lo hi , H return np.array o 0 for o in out , np.array o 1 for o in out def fit_first_order_delay

text: summary “Crisper,” “softer,” “it wobbles,” “it runs hot” — pilot feelings that can be turned into numbers from the log so you can compare profiles honestly. This module gives you a working method: filters before PID, one parameter per step, four profiles in one flight, five per-maneuver metrics. The case study is an experiment on two identical 7" drones: four profiles, what matched the feelings, what didn't, and why the outcome was not a new PID but new filters. theory Order: filters first, then PID PID amplifies everything that comes from the gyro, noise included. Tuning PID on bad filters is like tuning an amplifier against a background of interference. So: the RPM filter and the dynamic notch are working, the spectrum is clean the filter and RPM filter modules , and only then — PID. Betaflight 4.3+ sliders The simplified tuning mode turns groups of parameters at once: - Damping D — resistance to fast movements, damps overshoot; higher — the motors heat up. - Tracking P and I — how precisely it follows the stick and disturbances; higher — oscillations. - Stick Response FF — response to fast stick movements; higher — overshoot at the end of a flip. - Dynamic Damping D max — how much D can grow on fast moves. - Drift – Wobble I — holding in turns and at zero throttle. - Master Multiplier — everything at once; you touch it when the others run out of travel. In the CLI these are simplified_pi_gain , simplified_d_gain , simplified_feedforward_gain , simplified_dmax_gain in 2025.12 — simplified_d_max_gain , simplified_i_gain , simplified_master_multiplier plus simplified_tuning apply . There are four PID profiles and four rate profiles — switched from a switch or in the CLI with the profile N command. {{widget:pid-sim}} Symptoms - P too high — twitchy, overcorrects, fast oscillation. Too low — sluggish, slow wobble. - I too high — “robotic,” low-frequency oscillation. Too low — drifts off, “skates like on ice.” - D too low — bounce-back after flips, propwash on descents. Too high — hot motors, mushy response. - FF too high — overshoot at the start of a flip, jitter on stick movements. Check motor temperature after every change to D or the filters: a short flight, land, finger on the motor. If you can't hold it — roll back. Five per-maneuver metrics A maneuver is a segment where setpoint is above a threshold for example, 200 °/s for longer than 50 ms. For each one: Feeling Metric How to compute --- --- --- runs hot motor noise std of motor commands above 40 Hz, averaged over motors shakes on descent propwash RMS gyro RMS in the 20–70 Hz band on descent segments wobbles after a stop bounce-back opposite-sign gyro peak within 150 ms after the stop / maneuver amplitude, % slow on the stick entry lag time from the start of setpoint movement to 50% on gyro, ms undershoots / overshoots peak tracking max gyro / max setpoint, % The median over 10–20 maneuvers is robust; one bad snap ruins the mean. The classic step response Blackbox Explorer; PID-Analyzer — not developed since 2019, PIDscope works well on long freestyle logs, but on short logs of 1–2 minutes per profile it is noisy to ±40% — direct metrics are more honest. Case study: four profiles on two 7" drones Two nearly identical 7" drones same frame, motors, props, FC , brought to a common baseline. The four profiles differed only in sliders; filters were the same: COOL SHARP WASH FLOAT --- --- --- --- --- Tracking 1.00 1.15 1.00 1.00 Damping 1.00 1.00 1.20 0.85 D max 1.00 1.00 1.20 1.00 Feedforward 1.00 1.15 1.00 0.80 Result drone A, medians : motor noise 16.1 / 23.3 / 18.0 / 14.6; bounce-back 6.0 / 8.5 / 9.4 / 14.9%; entry lag 38 / 31 / 40 / 44 ms. - SHARP “crisper” — yes: lag is 7 ms lower. The price — motor noise +45%. That's P: it raises the gain at all frequencies. - FLOAT “softer” — yes, the quietest. But bounce-back is almost 15%: after a stop the drone rolls back by 1/7 of the amplitude. Bad for filming. - WASH “didn't feel a difference” — and the numbers confirmed it: propwash 0.97 of COOL, within the noise. At 1.4 kg on 7" props, propwash is aerodynamics, not underdamping. The profile was dropped. - The two “identical” drones gave different bounce-back on SHARP 2.9% vs. 8.5% : on the second one the pilot flew harder, and D-max had time to kick in. The lesson about the method: compare profiles only within a single flight or normalize to the maneuver amplitude. Outcome: COOL is the best compromise. Crispness was brought back not through P but through the filters: simplified_gyro_filter_multiplier 1.00 → 1.10 and dyn_notch_q 400 → 450, PID as in COOL. That's how the CRISP profile came about. The first proposal was more aggressive 1.25 and a single notch ; it was rejected in favor of small steps: 1.10 → flight → if successful, 1.20. Tuning protocol by data, not by feel 1. Baseline : 4.5 defaults, filters per the “Filters” module, clean spectrum, cold motors. Log A: 30 s hover + 10 maneuvers with a sharp stop on roll/pitch + 3 descents with propwash. 2. Metrics from log A data-python : step_metrics , bounce_back , motor noise, propwash RMS — into a table. 3. One slider per flight : Damping ±0.1 → log → metrics; then Tracking ±0.1; then Stick Response. Acceptance criterion: the target metric improved, the others didn't get worse, the motors aren't hotter. 4. A profile for the job : racing higher Tracking, higher Stick Response and calm higher Damping — different profile s, switched from a switch. 5. Lock it in : diff all + a “what — why — metrics before/after” table in the repository the “CI” module . One flight — one change. Two changes in one flight make the log useless. Metric reference values for 5" 6S Metric Good Tolerable Problem --- --- --- --- overshoot 3–10% 10–20% 20% P/FF bounce-back < 8% 8–15% 15% D, delay entry lag to 50% 20–35 ms 35–50 50 FF, filters settle ±5% < 80 ms 80–150 150 motor noise std 40 Hz low, stable grows with D “grass” on the motor trace motor temperature warm too hot to touch for 5 s can't hold a finger on it

text: summary The Betaflight command line CLI is a text interface that gives you access to the flight controller's configuration at a level the graphical interface doesn't offer. From the CLI you can change any parameter, including ones not exposed on the configurator tabs, check the hardware state, manage resources microcontroller pins and make backups. The key practical goal of this article is to give you confident command of resource and pin remapping without reflashing, and to teach you to inspect what is in the firmware build and restore the configuration after a failure. theory CLI architecture The CLI runs over a serial port UART , using the same channel as the configurator MSP , MultiWii Serial Protocol . To enter the CLI from a terminal e.g. PuTTY/screen , send the character — it switches the controller into command mode. Key commands and what they do - Session control: save , exit , batch start , batch end - Viewing the configuration: get , diff , dump , status , version - Changing parameters: set , feature , profile , rateprofile - Resource remapping: resource , timer - Troubleshooting and debugging: tasks , flash_info , dma Diff vs Dump: what to use and when diff all prints only the changed parameters. It is the main format for backups and for safe transfer within the same firmware version. dump all prints a full snapshot of the configuration, including default values. It suits deep troubleshooting, but is dangerous to carry between different versions. It is recommended to save separately: - diff all - resource show - status version/build Resource remapping: concept and limits The resource command manages the “function - physical pin” binding: text resource <FUNCTION <INDEX <PIN resource MOTOR 1 B00 resource MOTOR 5 NONE - ADC resources ADC_BATT , ADC_CURR , ADC_RSSI can only be assigned to ADC pins. - UARTs are limited by the controller's hardware blocks — not every pin can be used as a serial port. - For DShot, timers and DMA are critical: a wrong pin/channel leaves the motors dead. Betaflight 4.5 specifics Between versions, the names and logic of some parameters change: - D-term naming: in 4.5 d_roll is the peak D and d_min_roll is the base; in 2025.12 it's the other way round: d_roll is the base and d_max_roll is the peak d_min_ were removed . - GPS rescue: some variables were reworked. - Failsafe landing: differences in naming/behavior appeared. Because of this, you can't mindlessly paste old backups into new firmware. Checking the build contents via BUILD KEY In Betaflight 4.5+ status shows a BUILD KEY . Put it into the URL below and you get JSON with the list of enabled options Options : text https://build.betaflight.com/api/builds/<BUILD_KEY /json This helps diagnose missing features e.g. GPS/LED/VTX without reflashing. The recipes you need most often commands from cli/cli.c Task Command --- --- Find the version, target / BUILD KEY version / status CPU load, arming flags, gyro rate status , tasks Move a motor to another pad resource MOTOR 3 B01 → save resource show all — what's in use Change the motor order without resoldering resource pair swap, or “Motor direction/remap” on the Motors tab Reverse one motor's direction DShot commands dshotprog 0 21 21 — reversed, 20 — normal; on some ESCs 7/8 — direction 1/2 , then dshotprog 0 12 save settings ; motors without props, index from 0 255 — all motors Check DShot telemetry dshot_telemetry_info Timers/DMA motor, LED, serial conflicts timer , dma show Reset to defaults without saving / with saving defaults nosave , defaults Enter the DFU bootloader bl or bl rom Flash as a USB drive pulling logs msc Flash/configure ESCs serialpassthrough / escprog via the ESC configurator Batch-load a diff without intermediate reboots batch start … batch end → save Channel ranges, stick map rxrange , map AETR1234 Profiles profile 1 , rateprofile 2 Betaflight has no battery_profile command Beeper/sound test, sensors beeper , play_sound , gyroregisters detected sensors are in the status output Board signature and identification board_name , manufacturer_id , mcu_id , signature Worked example: the motor 2 pad burned off An F405 board, the M2 pad came off. resource show all — free timer pads: LED_STRIP 1 A08 . Check timer A08 list — there's a timer with DMA; resource LED_STRIP 1 NONE , resource MOTOR 2 A08 , timer A08 AF1 if needed , dma pin A08 0 , save ; Motors tab — motor 2 spins in the right position, without props; diff all into the repo with a comment. If the pad's timer conflicts with the other motors' DShot one DMA group , dma show will reveal it, and bitbang DShot dshot_bitbang = ON works around some conflicts. {{diagram:bf-resource-remap Moving a motor to another pad: check the timer and DMA, free the old resource, assign the new one, save and check on the Motors tab.}} practice Getting into the CLI 1. Connect the flight controller over USB and open Betaflight Configurator. 2. Go to the CLI tab. 3. Click Connect if the connection didn't come up automatically. The terminal alternative: - connect to the port /dev/ttyACM0 on Linux or COMx on Windows ; - set the baud rate to 115200 ; - send the character. Making a full backup Before any changes, save the current state: text status version diff all resource show timer show Save the output to a file — it gives you: - the version and build; - the list of changed parameters; - resource assignments; - the timer configuration. Viewing and changing parameters Viewing: text get gyro_ get acc set dyn_notch_min_hz = 150 Changing: text set dyn_notch_min_hz = 150 set dyn_notch_q = 250 save For batch editing fewer reboots : text batch start set gyro_lpf1_static_hz = 0 set gyro_lpf2_static_hz = 300 set dterm_lpf2_static_hz = 150 batch end save Motor remapping: a full example Scenario: the FC is rotated 90° clockwise without changing the orientation in the firmware. text:
summary Once you have more than one drone, configuring them by clicking around in Configurator is a road to mistakes. The Betaflight CLI is available over an ordinary serial port, which means you can script it. This module shows a working Python template pyserial and collects the pitfalls we actually stepped on while configuring several quadcopters in bulk: floating COM ports, “silent” parameter corrections, reboots and diff incompatibility between versions. theory How entering the CLI works Over USB, a flight controller is a virtual COM port USB CDC . The baud rate in the port settings doesn't matter for USB CDC; 115200 is the convention. The character puts the controller into the CLI, exit leaves it with a reboot. While the FC is in the CLI, no signal goes to the motors — the ESCs may beep, that's normal. Pitfall 1: the COM port isn't fixed If several identical boards are connected to the computer, they share one USB VID/PID, and the COM port number changes after every reboot. You can't bind to COM8 . The reliable identifier is the craft_name inside the config: open each port, enter the CLI, run get craft_name and pick the right one. Hence the rule: every drone gets a distinct craft_name before you start working. Pitfall 2: exit noreboot reboots In Betaflight 4.5.0–4.5.3 the exit command always reboots the controller the noreboot argument appeared in 4.5.4 and 2025.12.x . So after any exit the script has to find the port again by craft_name . When you “just want to peek at a value”, don't leave the CLI with a command — just close the port. Pitfall 3: silent corrections set + save doesn't guarantee that the value stayed the way you wrote it. On boot, Betaflight corrects incompatible combinations: the DShot protocol, bidirectional DShot, the timer layout on a specific board. In our practice, on an F405 board, after enabling bidir the DShot protocol turned out not to be what we had written. Rule: after every save and reboot, re-read every changed value with get and compare it with the expected one. Pitfall 4: a diff doesn't carry over between versions Parameter names and meanings change between firmware versions: debug_mode values get renamed, the serial command syntax changes, the meaning of the D-term PID parameters changes. You can't paste a diff all from 2025.12 into 4.5 or vice versa line by line. Moving settings between versions only works deliberately, section by section, with re-reading. Why diff and not dump diff all contains only the differences from defaults — you can read it by eye and keep it in git. dump is everything at once; when you update the firmware it drags the old defaults along as explicit values. Minimal script for exporting diff all pyserial python import serial, time, sys, glob def cli port, cmds, timeout=3.0 : """Open CLI, run commands, return full text. Do not send 'exit' reboots on 4.5 .""" with serial.Serial port, 115200, timeout=0.2 as s: s.write b" 
" ; time.sleep 0.5 ; s.read s.in_waiting or 1 out = "" for c in cmds: s.write c + "
" .encode ; t0 = time.time ; buf = "" while time.time - t0 < timeout: chunk = s.read 4096 .decode errors="replace" if chunk: buf += chunk; t0 = time.time if buf.rstrip .endswith " " : break prompt returned out += buf return out ports = glob.glob "/dev/ttyACM " Linux; Windows: COM for p in ports: name = cli p, "get craft_name" if "viking7" in name: text = cli p, "version", "diff all" open "viking7/betaflight/diff-all.txt", "w" .write text break else: sys.exit "craft not found" Normalize before committing: strip the date/time lines from version and the echo, sort the blocks — otherwise git diff gets noisy the “CI” module . What's worth automating and what isn't Worth it: a diff all backup before every flying day; checking invariants failsafe, poles, bidir from the export; bulk changes of craft_name /VTX table across the fleet; downloading logs via msc . Not worth it: bulk “rolling out PIDs” to different vehicles different mechanics , any change without re-reading with get after save . {{diagram:bf-cli-session A CLI session over serial: wait for the prompt, re-read values after set, find the port again after save.}} practice Step 1.
