title: IMU sensors: physics, errors, calibration
summary: The autopilot knows about the world only what its sensors tell it, and each of them lies in its own way. This module covers the physics of the MEMS gyroscope, accelerometer and magnetometer at the level an engineer needs: bias (zero offset), noise (ARW/VRW), temperature drift, scale error and non-or
headings: MEMS gyroscope MEMS accelerometer 6-position accelerometer calibration Magnetometer Barometer (briefly; more in the altitude module) What the firmware does with raw data Step 1. Gyro noise and bias at rest Step 2. Temperature drift Step 3. Accelerometer calibration Step 4. Compass: hard iron
text: summary The autopilot knows about the world only what its sensors tell it, and each of them lies in its own way. This module covers the physics of the MEMS gyroscope, accelerometer and magnetometer at the level an engineer needs: bias zero offset , noise ARW/VRW , temperature drift, scale error and non-orthogonality; what exactly the 6-position accelerometer calibration and the compass calibration hard/soft iron calibrate, and how to measure gyro bias and noise yourself. The result is an “IMU datasheet” for your own flight controller, with numbers. theory MEMS gyroscope A vibrating mass inside the chip; when the body rotates, the Coriolis force deflects it perpendicularly, and a capacitive sensor measures the deflection, which is proportional to angular rate. The output is three angular rates in °/s or rad/s , with a typical range of ±2000 °/s ICM42688: up to ±2000, 16 bits → 0.061 °/s per LSB . Errors: - Bias b — the output at zero rotation: a few °/s “out of the box”; after zero calibration on the ground ArduPilot — at power-up INS_GYR_CAL = 1 , Start-up only , Betaflight — at power-up what remains is bias instability of 0.01–0.1 °/s, which wanders with time and temperature. When you integrate ω to get an angle, a 0.05 °/s bias gives 3° per minute — that's why you can't get the angle from the gyro alone. - Noise — white, characterized by Angle Random Walk: ARW ≈ 0.1–0.5 °/√h for consumer MEMS; in a 1 kHz bandwidth that's ~0.1 °/s RMS. On a spectrum it's the flat floor that the motor peaks sit on. - Temperature drift of the bias: 0.01–0.05 °/s per °C; the board warming up by 20 °C after power-up causes a noticeable shift. ArduPilot: INS_TCAL_ temperature calibration , IMU heating on the Cube/some H7 boards BRD_HEAT_TARG . - Scale and non-orthogonality : a 0.5–1% error — over a 360° rotation that's a 2–4° error; rarely calibrated you need a rate table . - g-sensitivity : linear acceleration vibration! changes the output — yet another path by which vibration corrupts the estimate. MEMS accelerometer A proof mass on a spring; it measures specific force : at rest it reads +1 g upward the support reaction force , in free fall — 0. Hence the key fact: the accelerometer does not measure motion acceleration separately from gravity; in a steady hover it sees ~1 g along the vehicle's “up,” and in a coordinated turn — also along “up” which is why the roll angle from the accelerometer is wrong in a turn . Errors: bias tens of mg, i.e., a 1–3° horizon error without calibration , scale 1–2% , axis non-orthogonality, temperature drift, clipping saturation at ±16 g from impacts and vibration — VIBE.Clip in ArduPilot , vibration aliasing into the band. 6-position accelerometer calibration The vehicle is placed on 6 faces ±X, ±Y, ±Z up . In each one the truth is known: exactly +1 g on one axis, 0 on the others. From the six measurements you solve a system for 3 biases + 3 scales ArduPilot also solves for non-orthogonality during INS_ACC _ID calibration via Mission Planner . Betaflight calibrates only the zero from a single position level — the scale error remains, but for Acro it doesn't matter. Rule: calibrate at the temperature you fly at; after a hard crash, redo it. Magnetometer Measures the magnetic field µT or mGauss on three axes; the heading is the projection of the Earth's field ~25–65 µT, inclination up to 70° at mid-latitudes — a large vertical component, which is why the heading is wrong without knowing roll/pitch . - Hard iron — a constant field from magnetized parts and DC currents on board: it shifts the measurement sphere away from the origin. Calibrated as an offset COMPASS_OFS_ ; the “compass dance” — rotating about all axes to fill the sphere. - Soft iron — ferromagnetic materials distort the field: the sphere becomes an ellipsoid. Calibrated with a matrix COMPASS_DIA_ , COMPASS_ODI_ . - Current-induced interference see the EMI module : depends on throttle → compassmot , COMPASS_MOT_ . - Compass orientation relative to the FC COMPASS_ORIENT — a common mistake with an external compass; ArduPilot can detect it automatically during calibration. Barometer briefly; more in the altitude module Pressure → altitude via the standard atmosphere; errors: temperature drift, prop airflow, weather 1–3 m drift in half an hour , solar heating. Resolution of good MEMS baros is ~10 cm, noise ~0.5 m unfiltered. What the firmware does with raw data ArduPilot: INS_GYRO_FILTER / INS_ACCEL_FILTER 20 Hz LPF for accel by default , notches, then EKF3 estimates gyro and accelerometer bias in flight EKF states: XKF1.GX/GY/GZ — gyro bias, XKF2.AX/AY/AZ — accel bias . Betaflight — filters and a complementary attitude filter the “Attitude” module . {{diagram:imu-error-model MEMS error model: calibration removes scale and misalignment, the EKF estimates the bias, and mechanics and filters deal with noise and vibration.}} practice Step 1. Gyro noise and bias at rest A 60 s log on the ground, motors off ArduPilot: LOG_DISARMED = 1 , IMU ; Betaflight: blackbox with blackbox_mode = ALWAYS or via a switch . For each of the three axes: the mean bias after zero calibration and the std noise . Expected: bias < 0.1 °/s, std 0.05–0.3 °/s at 1 kHz. Step 2. Temperature drift The same log right after powering up a cold board and again after 10 minutes of warm-up: the shift in the mean. If it's 0.2 °/s, enable/check temperature calibration or heating. Step 3. Accelerometer calibration 6-position via Mission Planner / QGC ArduPilot or level + calibration in Betaflight. Check: level with a spirit level on the frame! , AHRS roll/pitch ≤ 0.5°; on its side — 90 ± 1°. Step 4. Compass: hard iron Before calibration: record MAG.MagX/Y/Z while slowly rotating 360° level → a circle on the MagX–MagY plot; the center of the circle = the hard-iron offset. After calibration, COMPASS_OFS_ should roughly match the center you found. Record the field magnitude B — it should be constant within ±5% at any orientation. Lab: an IMU datasheet with bias/n

title: Attitude: Euler angles, quaternions, complementary filter
summary: “Which way is up” is the first question an autopilot answers a thousand times per second. The gyro gives a fast but drifting answer; the accelerometer a slow and noisy one, but without drift; the compass gives heading. This module explains why Euler angles break (gimbal lock) and firmware lives on q
headings: Representing attitude Integrating the gyro Complementary filter What this is in firmware Why yaw is special Step 1. Recording the IMU Step 2. Your own filter Step 3. Experiments Step 4. Yaw What you should get and what to record
text: summary “Which way is up” is the first question an autopilot answers a thousand times per second. The gyro gives a fast but drifting answer; the accelerometer a slow and noisy one, but without drift; the compass gives heading. This module explains why Euler angles break gimbal lock and firmware lives on quaternions, how to integrate angular rate, how a complementary filter works in Python, ~40 lines and how it relates to ArduPilot's DCM and to Mahony/Madgwick in Betaflight/INAV. Lab: your own filter on an IMU recording against ATT from the log. theory Representing attitude - Euler angles roll φ, pitch θ, yaw ψ — convenient for humans. The problem: at θ = ±90° roll and yaw merge gimbal lock , and the equations for the angle rates contain a division by cos θ. For freestyle with loops that's unacceptable. They're used only for output ATT.Roll/Pitch/Yaw . - Rotation matrix DCM — 3×3, the columns are the aircraft axes in the earth frame. No singularities, but 9 numbers with 6 constraints; it needs orthonormalization after integration. - Quaternion q = w, x, y, z , q = 1 — 4 numbers, one constraint, no singularities, cheap multiplication. The standard in Betaflight since 3.x , INAV, PX4 vehicle_attitude.q , EKF3 states 0–3 . Quaternion → Euler conversion for output : φ = atan2 2 wx + yz , 1 − 2 x² + y² ; θ = asin 2 wy − zx ; ψ = atan2 2 wz + xy , 1 − 2 y² + z² . {{widget:attitude-3d}} Integrating the gyro Angular rate ω in body axes changes the quaternion: q̇ = ½ · q ⊗ 0, ω . Discretely over a step Δt: q ← q ⊗ cos ω Δt/2 , ω/ ω · sin ω Δt/2 , then normalize. Gyro only → drift at the bias rate 0.05 °/s → 3°/min plus accumulated noise. Complementary filter The idea: trust the gyro at high frequencies and the accelerometer gravity at low frequencies. The Mahony algorithm: 1. Predict “down” in body axes from the current q: v = R q ᵀ · 0, 0, 1 . 2. The measured “down” is the normalized accelerometer with a minus sign: −a/ a the accelerometer measures specific force; at rest in FRD it reads 0, 0, −g . 3. The error is the cross product e = a × v small when they agree; its direction is the correction axis . 4. Correct the angular rate: ω' = ω + Kp·e + Ki·∫e Ki is the gyro bias estimate! . 5. Integrate ω' into q. Kp sets the time constant of “trust” in the accelerometer: τ ≈ 1/Kp; Kp = 0.5 → ~2 s. During maneuvers a ≠ 1 g — the accelerometer lies; the standard protection is to reduce Kp when a − g is large ArduPilot DCM: AHRS_GPS_GAIN , using GPS for centripetal correction; Betaflight: imu_dcm_kp , disabling correction under large accelerations . The compass is added the same way for the yaw axis: the error between the measured and expected direction of the field's horizontal component. What this is in firmware - Betaflight : a Mahony-like quaternion filter, imu_dcm_kp default 2500 → 0.25 after scaling , imu_dcm_ki ; without a compass yaw drifts — irrelevant for Acro, and GPS Rescue uses the GPS course. - INAV : the same class of filter + compass and GPS course, corrections that account for acceleration from GPS. - ArduPilot : DCM a matrix, with correction from GPS velocity as the fallback; the primary one is EKF3 , where attitude is part of the state vector together with velocity, position and sensor biases. A complementary filter is an EKF with constant, non-adaptive gains. - PX4 : EKF2 ekf2 , attitude in vehicle_attitude . Why yaw is special Gravity carries no information about heading: without a compass or GPS course, yaw drifts with the gyro Z bias. In a hover that's ~3°/min, unnoticeable; over 10 minutes it's 30°, and Loiter will spiral the “toilet bowl” is the classic symptom . Yaw sources: compass interference , GPS course while moving not in a hover , dual GPS moving baseline , EKF-GSF estimation from motion, ArduPilot EK3_SRC1_YAW = 8 , external navigation. {{diagram:complementary-filter Complementary filter: the gyro integral is accurate over a short interval, the accelerometer angle over a long one; the weights α and 1 − α blend them.}} practice Step 1. Recording the IMU ArduPilot: a log with IMU gyro, accel and ATT ; LOG_BITMASK with IMU_RAW isn't needed — 50–400 Hz IMU is enough. Betaflight: blackbox with debug_mode = ATTITUDE it logs the angles , or use gyro + accel from a regular log. A 2–3 minute flight with tilts and hovering. Step 2. Your own filter python import numpy as np def qmul a, b : w1,x1,y1,z1 = a; w2,x2,y2,z2 = b return np.array w1 w2-x1 x2-y1 y2-z1 z2, w1 x2+x1 w2+y1 z2-z1 y2, w1 y2-x1 z2+y1 w2+z1 x2, w1 z2+x1 y2-y1 x2+z1 w2 def down_body q : gravity direction in body frame from quaternion w,x,y,z w,x,y,z = q return np.array 2 x z - w y , 2 w x + y z , w w - x x - y y + z z def mahony gyro, acc, dt, kp=0.5, ki=0.01 : q = np.array 1.0, 0, 0, 0 ; ib = np.zeros 3 ; out = for g, a in zip gyro, acc : g in rad/s, a in m/s^2 body frame an = np.linalg.norm a if an 1e-3: a_u = -a / an; v = down_body q accel measures specific force -g at rest, FRD e = np.cross a_u, v trust = 1.0 if abs an - 9.81 < 2.0 else 0.0 ignore accel during hard manoeuvres ib += ki e dt trust g = g + kp e trust + ib n = np.linalg.norm g if n 1e-9: dq = np.concatenate np.cos n dt/2 , g/n np.sin n dt/2 q = qmul q, dq ; q /= np.linalg.norm q w,x,y,z = q out.append np.degrees np.arctan2 2 w x+y z , 1-2 x x+y y , np.degrees np.arcsin np.clip 2 w y-z x , -1, 1 return np.array out Run it on your own recording; plot roll/pitch against ATT.Roll/Pitch ArduPilot or the angles from the debug log. Step 3. Experiments - Ki = 0: watch the slow drift under a constant bias. - Kp = 0: gyro only — drift. - Kp = 5: the accelerometer “pulls” during maneuvers — errors while accelerating. - Compare the RMS error relative to ATT for the three Kp values. Step 4. Yaw Integrate gyro Z without correction — record the drift over a minute; compare with ATT.Yaw . Explain where the firmware gets its heading from. Lab: the filter is implemented, compared with ATT, the yaw drift is explained. What you should get and what to record - Comparison

title: The Kalman filter in plain terms, and the EKF
summary: EKF3 in ArduPilot and EKF2 in PX4 are the same trick repeated for 24 states. This module explains it in one dimension: prediction from the model, correction from the measurement, covariance as “how unsure I am,” the Kalman gain as the compromise between the two, and the innovation as the “expected v
headings: The problem One Kalman step (scalar) Worked example: two steps by hand Q and R: what they mean and how to tune them Observability: what the filter can learn at all Delays: the filter lives in the past Why this beats a complementary filter Innovations and gates What's in the EKF3 state vector Parameters worth touching Step 1. A 1D altitude filter Step 1b. The Q and R knobs Step 2. A barometer outlier Step 3. Connecting to the log
text: summary EKF3 in ArduPilot and EKF2 in PX4 are the same trick repeated for 24 states. This module explains it in one dimension: prediction from the model, correction from the measurement, covariance as “how unsure I am,” the Kalman gain as the compromise between the two, and the innovation as the “expected vs. observed” difference. You implement a 1D altitude filter from barometer and accelerometer ~30 lines , see what it does when the barometer produces an outlier, and how this looks in the log: XKF4.SV/SP/SH/SM normalized innovations , XKF3 innovations , XKF1/XKF2 states, bias . theory The problem You have a motion model how the state evolves on its own and measurements noisy, sometimes infrequent . You want a state estimate better than either of the two alone, plus an honest estimate of its uncertainty. One Kalman step scalar State x e.g., altitude , uncertainty P variance of the estimate . 1. Prediction : x⁻ = f x from the model: x + v·Δt , P⁻ = P + Q, where Q is the process noise “how wrong the model can be over one step” . 2. Innovation : y = z − h x⁻ — the measurement minus what you expected. S = P⁻ + R is its variance R is the measurement noise . 3. Gain : K = P⁻ / S ∈ 0, 1 . If the measurement is accurate small R , K → 1 and you trust the measurement; if the model is accurate small P⁻ , K → 0 and you ignore the measurement. 4. Correction : x = x⁻ + K·y, P = 1 − K ·P⁻. Everything else is the same scheme with vectors and matrices: P is the covariance matrix, H describes how the state turns into a measurement, K = P Hᵀ H P Hᵀ + R ⁻¹. Extended EKF means the model is nonlinear rotations via a quaternion , and it is linearized around the current point Jacobians . Worked example: two steps by hand Altitude is unknown: x = 0 m, P = 4 m² σ = 2 m — “roughly, give or take two meters” . The barometer has noise R = 1 m². 1. A reading z = 10 m arrives. Prediction with no motion: x⁻ = 0, P⁻ = 4 Q = 0 . S = 4 + 1 = 5, K = 4/5 = 0.8. Innovation y = 10. x = 0 + 0.8·10 = 8 m , P = 0.2·4 = 0.8 m² . The measurement is four times more precise than our guess — and it got 80 % of the weight. 2. One step passes, and the model allows drift Q = 0.1: P⁻ = 0.9. A reading z = 9 m arrives: S = 1.9, K = 0.47, y = 1, x = 8 + 0.47 = 8.47 m , P = 0.53·0.9 = 0.47 m² . The point: K dropped from 0.8 to 0.47 on its own, because the estimate got more precise. After a dozen measurements K will be ~0.1–0.3 and stop falling: Q “pumps up” the uncertainty every step, R keeps it from reaching zero, and an equilibrium sets in. That is exactly what the chart below shows. Q and R: what they mean and how to tune them - R is the rated measurement noise: barometer variance at rest, the σ² of GPS position grows with HDOP . You can measure it: log on the ground, take the signal variance. - Q is how far reality can drift from the model in one step: unmodeled accelerations, bias drift. You cannot measure it directly — it is a tuning knob. - Q too small → the filter is “overconfident”: K is small, the estimate lags behind maneuvers, innovations are systematically large, and if the gates are narrow, measurements start getting rejected and the filter diverges. - Q too large → the filter is “jittery”: K is close to 1, the estimate repeats the measurement noise, and the model is pointless. - Honesty check: the normalized innovation y/√S should be ~N 0, 1 , i.e., its square should average ≈ 1 the NIS test . A mean of 5 means the filter underestimates its uncertainty Q or R too small ; 0.1 means it overestimates it. Observability: what the filter can learn at all You can only estimate what affects the measurements. The Z accelerometer bias is visible because the baro “catches” the altitude drift. Heading without a compass is unobservable in a hover: GPS velocity is zero, and you can turn 180° — the measurements are the same. That is why ArduPilot runs a separate heading estimator based on GPS velocity in motion GSF , and with COMPASS_USE = 0 the EKF waits for the vehicle to pick up speed. Rule of thumb: if a state is unobservable, its P grows, and you see it in the log before you see it in flight. Delays: the filter lives in the past GPS arrives with a 100–200 ms delay, and so do optical flow and external navigation. EKF3 and EKF2 therefore run the filter on a “delayed time horizon”: a measurement is fused with the state at the moment it was taken, and for the control loops the current state is propagated forward using the IMU output predictor . A wrong delay GPS1_DELAY_MS , EK3_FLOW_DELAY is the classic reason innovations grow during maneuvers and drop in a hover. Why this beats a complementary filter A complementary filter is a Kalman filter with a fixed K. A real Kalman filter adjusts K itself: when GPS gives bad data large R from HDOP , trust drops; when there have been no measurements for a while, P grows and the very first measurement is accepted with a large weight. And it estimates sensor biases as states — what Ki does blindly in a complementary filter. Innovations and gates An innovation y with variance S gives the normalized quantity y²/S. In ArduPilot, XKF4.SV/SP/SH/SM velocity, position, height, compass are the square root of the test ratio, i.e., the ratio “innovation / maximum allowed innovation” itself, where the allowance is set by the gates EK3_VEL_I_GATE , EK3_HGT_I_GATE , EK3_MAG_I_GATE , in percent of σ : < 1 — the measurement is accepted, 1 — it is rejected . A healthy flight shows values < 0.5. This is protection against GPS and compass outliers: one bad sample won't break the estimate. But if measurements are consistently outside the gates, the filter “drifts away” on the model until it resets lane switch, reset, EKF failsafe . What's in the EKF3 state vector 24 states: quaternion 4 , NED velocity 3 , NED position 3 , gyro bias 3 , accelerometer bias 3 , Earth field NED 3 , body field 3 , NE wind 2 . Measurements: GPS position/velocity, baro, compass, airspeed, rangefinder, optical flow, external navigation, beacons,

title: GNSS: how GPS works, errors, RTK
summary: For an autopilot, GPS isn't a “dot on the map” but a noisy measurement with a known (and changing) error. This module explains how a receiver gets pseudoranges and solves for position, where the errors come from (the ionosphere, multipath, satellite geometry — HDOP), what multiple constellations giv
headings: The principle Errors and their magnitudes (single-frequency receiver, good conditions) DOP: geometry Constellations Antenna u-blox settings that matter RTK and PPK How GPS enters the EKF Step 1. Three conditions Step 2. Multipath Step 3. Settings Step 4. Assessing the need for RTK Script: position scatter in place What you should get and what to record
text: summary For an autopilot, GPS isn't a “dot on the map” but a noisy measurement with a known and changing error. This module explains how a receiver gets pseudoranges and solves for position, where the errors come from the ionosphere, multipath, satellite geometry — HDOP , what multiple constellations give you GPS, GLONASS, Galileo, BeiDou , how to choose a receiver and an antenna, which u-blox settings matter for flight rate, constellations, dynamic model, SBAS , and what RTK/PPK are, when you need them and when you don't. Lab: GPS quality under different conditions, from the log. theory The principle Each satellite transmits time and its orbit; the receiver measures the signal delay → pseudorange distance + receiver clock error . Four unknowns x, y, z, Δt → at least 4 satellites; more is better redundancy, quality estimation . The signal at the input is ~−130 dBm — weaker than the noise; it's extracted by correlating with a known code. Errors and their magnitudes single-frequency receiver, good conditions Source Error How to reduce it --- --- --- Ionosphere 2–5 m dual frequency L1+L5/L2 , SBAS correction Troposphere 0.5–1 m model Satellite orbit/clock 1–2 m SBAS Multipath reflections from buildings, the ground, the frame 1–10+ m, in jumps antenna with a ground plane, higher above the frame, away from structures Geometry DOP multiplier ×1–×5 many satellites across the whole sky Receiver noise 0.3–1 m a good antenna, no interference Total: 1.5–3 m CEP in an open field, 5–20 m in a city. Velocity from Doppler is much more accurate — 0.05–0.2 m/s; the EKF relies on it more than on position. DOP: geometry HDOP horizontal is an error multiplier from the satellite layout: all satellites on one side of the sky → bad. < 1 is excellent, 1–2 is good; above the threshold ArduPilot won't arm in GPS modes GPS_HDOP_GOOD , stored as HDOP × 100; default 140 = 1.4 . Satellite count is a rough indicator: 6 is the minimum, 12+ is normal with multiple constellations. Constellations GPS USA, L1 C/A , GLONASS Russia , Galileo EU, L1 + E5 , BeiDou China . A multi-constellation receiver u-blox M8/M9/M10, F9P sees 20–30 satellites instead of 8–10: better DOP, faster fix, more robust when part of the sky is blocked. The cost is computational load and update rate: M8 — 10 Hz with 2–3 constellations, M9/M10 — up to 25 Hz, F9P — 20 Hz RTK. Antenna A 25×25 mm ceramic patch on a ground plane is the standard; helical antennas are circularly polarized, better against multipath, and don't need a ground plane. The rule: antenna on top, on a mast, nothing metal nearby, ground plane ≥ 40 mm for a patch. An active antenna with an amplifier is for a long cable. u-blox settings that matter - Rate : 5–10 Hz for a copter ArduPilot GPS_RATE_MS = 200 , in 4.6+ GPS1_RATE_MS → 5 Hz; the EKF doesn't need more, and it overloads the UART/CPU . - Dynamic model : Airborne < 1g/2g/4g — the filter inside the receiver tuned for the dynamics; Pedestrian/Automotive are bad for a drone they smooth and lag . ArduPilot sets GPS_NAVFILTER . - Constellations GPS_GNSS_MODE : GPS + Galileo + GLONASS or GPS + Galileo + BeiDou — not all four at once on an M8 the rate drops . - SBAS GPS_SBAS_MODE : WAAS/EGNOS corrections — slightly more accurate, but in some regions it gets in the way; enable it where there is coverage. - Messages : UBX binary instead of NMEA — more compact, more precise, with quality status; ArduPilot configures a u-blox receiver itself with GPS_AUTO_CONFIG = 1 . RTK and PPK RTK Real-Time Kinematic : a base station at a known position sends carrier-phase corrections RTCM to the rover receiver over radio/4G; accuracy is 1–3 cm with a fix RTK Fixed status , 10–50 cm with float. You need a dual-frequency receiver F9P, UM982 on both ends, the base within ~10–20 km, and a continuous link. PPK is the same but post-processed from logs: it's for photogrammetry, not for flight control. When you need RTK: precision landing, surveying, moving baseline for heading two GPS units → yaw without a compass: ArduPilot “GPS for yaw,” base GPS_TYPE = 17 , rover GPS_TYPE2 = 18 ; in 4.6+ — GPS1_TYPE / GPS2_TYPE . When you don't: regular waypoint flying the EKF and a 2 m error are enough , FPV. RTK doesn't cure multipath or satellite loss under a roof. How GPS enters the EKF The EKF receives position, velocity, their accuracy estimates GPA.HAcc/VAcc/SAcc and the delay GPS1_DELAY_MS ~ 100–200 ms — the measurement is “old,” the EKF accounts for that . Quality is checked EK3_GPS_CHECK : HDOP, satellite count, velocity drift on the ground before arming is allowed in GPS modes. Glitch protection is the innovation gate see the Kalman module . {{diagram:rtk-chain A standard GNSS solution gives meters; RTCM corrections from a base at a known point give an RTK fix with centimeter accuracy.}} practice Step 1. Three conditions Ground logs, 5 minutes each LOG_DISARMED = 1 : an open field; next to a house wall; under trees. From GPS : NSats , HDop , Status ; from GPA : HAcc , SAcc . Table: the average and the worst for each condition. Step 2. Multipath For the second condition, plot the position GPS.Lat/Lng → meters over 5 minutes in place: the scatter and the jumps. Compare with the field. Match the jumps with XKF4.SP in the log normalized position innovation, √test ratio , if the EKF was running. Step 3. Settings Check GPS_RATE_MS , GPS_GNSS_MODE , GPS_NAVFILTER or the equivalents in INAV/Betaflight: gps_ublox_use_galileo , dynamic model , GPS_AUTO_CONFIG . Record them in the build logbook. Step 4. summary: The EKF is a filter that takes noisy and contradictory sensors and builds one consistent picture out of them: where the vehicle is, where it is going and how it is oriented. text: summary The EKF is a filter that takes noisy and contradictory sensors and builds one consistent picture out of them: where the vehicle is, where it is going and how it is oriented. When ArduPilot “won't arm because of the EKF”, “drifts in LOITER” or “flies away on a GPS glitch”, the cause is almost always here. This module explains what the filter does, how to choose data sources, what variances and lane switching are, and how to read its health in the GCS and in logs. A real-world example: a HeeWing with no compass and an unstable GPS. theory Why a filter A gyroscope is accurate over short intervals but drifts. GPS does not drift, but it is noisy and updates rarely. A barometer knows the altitude but lies in wind and when it heats up. A compass knows the heading but is afraid of current. The EKF extended Kalman filter predicts the state from the inertial sensors thousands of times per second and corrects the prediction with the infrequent GPS, baro and compass measurements, weighting them by their declared noise. A measurement too far from the prediction is rejected by the filter — that is how GPS glitches are handled. EKF3, DCM and lane switching - AHRS_EKF_TYPE = 3 — EKF3 is the main estimator; DCM a simple complementary filter runs in the background as a backup. - Each IMU in EK3_IMU_MASK gets its own core “lane” . The healthiest one is used; when one core degrades, the filter switches to another. EK3_PRIMARY selects the starting one. - Plane and Rover fall back to DCM when the EKF is unhealthy; Copter does not — it has the EKF failsafe instead. Sources Where position, velocity, altitude and heading come from is set by EK3_SRC1_ : {{diagram:estimation-sources EKF3 merges all the sensors into one estimate: the IMU drives the prediction, the other sources correct it through innovation gates.}} - EK3_SRC1_POSXY : 0 — none, 3 — GPS, 4 — Beacon, 6 — ExternalNav. - EK3_SRC1_VELXY : in addition 5 — OpticalFlow, 7 — WheelEncoder. - EK3_SRC1_POSZ : 1 — Baro, 2 — RangeFinder, 3 — GPS. - EK3_SRC1_YAW : 1 — Compass, 2 — GPS, 3 — GPS with fallback to compass, 8 — GSF heading estimated from GPS velocity without a compass . The SRC2 / SRC3 sets can be switched in flight with a switch — for example, GPS outdoors and optical flow indoors. Variances and failsafe The filter estimates its own uncertainty for compass, velocity, position and height. When the normalized variance exceeds FS_EKF_THRESH 0.8 by default, 0.6 is strict, 1.0 is lenient , the EKF failsafe triggers with the FS_EKF_ACTION action: 1 — land if the mode requires position; 2 — AltHold; 3 — land from any mode. The same variances are used in pre-arm: “EKF variance” at arming is a signal of a bad compass or GPS, not a reason to raise the threshold. What requires position LOITER, AUTO, GUIDED, RTL, PosHold need a healthy position estimate. STABILIZE, ALT_HOLD, ACRO do not. Hence the rule from the ArduPilot module: you choose the mode by which sensors you trust. Case: flying without a compass and without trusting GPS A HeeWing T1 on a stock F405: there is no compass on board at all, and GPS behaved erratically during setup. Instead of forcing the EKF to work with an unreliable heading, the decision was to disable EKF3 and fly on DCM: the vehicle arms and is controlled in modes that do not need position MANUAL, FBWA, ACRO, QSTABILIZE, QLAND , and altitude and position hold are deliberately not used. An alternative for the future, once GPS is stable: EK3_SRC1_YAW = 8 GSF — heading from GPS without a compass, but it only becomes available while moving. How to read EKF health from the log XKF4 per core : SV , SP , SH , SM — the square root of the test ratio, i.e. the ratio of the innovation to the allowed one by the gates EK3_VEL_I_GATE , EK3_POS_I_GATE , EK3_HGT_I_GATE , EK3_MAG_I_GATE , in % : < 0.5 — healthy, around 1 — the measurement is on the edge of rejection, 1 — rejected; SS — the solution status bitmask which sources are in use ; PI — the active core; XKF3 — the innovations themselves IVN/IVE/IVD velocity, IPN/IPE/IPD position, IMX/IMY/IMZ compass ; XKF2 — the estimated accelerometer bias, wind and magnetic field; XKF1 — the state angles, velocities, position and gyro bias GX/GY/GZ . The messages EKF3 IMU0 … yaw re-aligned , … ground mag anomaly are automatic resets normal if rare, suspicious if frequent . For the math in detail see the “Kalman Filter” module; for practical degradation scenarios see “Navigation Robustness”. Parameters people actually tune EK3_GPS_CHECK GPS quality checks before trusting it , GPS1_DELAY_MS / EK3_FLOW_DELAY / EK3_HGT_DELAY measurement delay, ms , EK3_ALT_SOURCE → EK3_SRC1_POSZ , EK3_RNG_USE_HGT % of height for the rangefinder , EK3_GLITCH_RAD 25 m: beyond that — reset to GPS , EK3_MAG_CAL when to calibrate the field in flight , EK3_FLOW_USE , EK3_SRC_OPTIONS . Measurement noise EK3_ _M_NSE and process noise EK3_ _P_NSE — only after you understand the Kalman module, and with before/after logs. Worked example: “EKF variance” in Loiter over a parking lot XKF4.SM = 1.3 and rising with throttle, MAG.MagZ correlates with CTUN.ThO , GPS.NSats 14, SP 0.2 → the compass is affected by the power wires the parking lot's metal is secondary . Solution: compassmot/moving the compass onto a mast the “Interference” module , EK3_SRC1_YAW = 3 GPS with fallback to compass as insurance; leave FS_EKF_THRESH alone. practice Checking EKF health 1. In Mission Planner — the EKF window a button on the HUD : the variance bars should be green and low. 2. In MAVProxy: the EKF3 IMU0 ... messages at startup — wait for “using GPS” before arming in position modes. 3. Pre-arm “EKF compass variance” or “EKF velocity variance” — look for the cause in the compass interference, calibration or GPS few satellites, HDOP . Lab in SITL: a GPS glitch 1. summary: Indoors, under tree canopy and next to walls GPS is useless, and the baro “breathes.” This module breaks down barometer errors and how they're compensated, what a rangefinder (lidar/ultrasonic/radar) and optical flow give you, how they're connected in ArduPilot and INAV, and how to use `EK3_SRCn_*`
headings: Barometer: where the errors come from Rangefinder Optical flow Building a source set INAV Step 1. Baro Step 2. Rangefinder Step 3. SITL without GPS Step 4. Bench/flight
text: summary Indoors, under tree canopy and next to walls GPS is useless, and the baro “breathes.” This module breaks down barometer errors and how they're compensated, what a rangefinder lidar/ultrasonic/radar and optical flow give you, how they're connected in ArduPilot and INAV, and how to use EK3_SRCn_ to build a source set for the job: indoors, forest, precision landing. The lab is position hold without GPS in SITL optical flow + rangefinder and on the bench. theory Barometer: where the errors come from Altitude from pressure via the standard atmosphere: Δh ≈ −8.4 m per 1 hPa near the ground. Errors: - Weather : pressure changes by 1–3 hPa per hour when a front passes → 10–25 m of drift per hour; relative altitude over a 10-minute flight is ±1–3 m. - Chip temperature : warm-up after power-on drifts by meters BARO_ calibration, ArduPilot TCAL_ENABLED / TCAL_BARO_EXP , foam for thermal stability . - Prop wash and airspeed : dynamic pressure ½ρv² — at 20 m/s that's 2.4 hPa ≈ 20 m! The baro must sit in a “quiet” spot, under foam; on wings — compensation from airspeed on copters — BARO1_WCF_ , wind pressure compensation; BARO_GND_TEMP is only the ground temperature used for the altitude calculation , on copters — the prop-wash effect on takeoff/landing −1…−3 m of false altitude near the ground . - Noise : 0.2–0.5 m RMS unfiltered. The EKF blends the baro with the accelerometer see the Kalman module : fast changes come from the accel, the slow level from the baro; nothing compensates the weather drift relative to the takeoff point except GPS altitude EK3_SRC1_POSZ = 3 or a rangefinder near the ground. Rangefinder - Lidar TFmini-S 12 m, TF02 40 m, Lightware SF20/LW20 100 m, Benewake TF03 180 m : narrow beam, works on any surface except black/mirror-like/water; error 1–3% or ±5 cm. - Ultrasonic MaxBotix : cheap, 5–7 m, noisy from props and wind, poor over grass. - Radar Ainstein, Nanoradar 60 GHz : 30–100 m, works over water and in dust, more expensive. Connection: UART SERIALx_PROTOCOL = 9 , RNGFND1_TYPE per model , I2C TFmini in I2C mode, RNGFND1_TYPE = 25 , DroneCAN RNGFND1_TYPE = 24 . Parameters: RNGFND1_MIN/MAX_CM , RNGFND1_ORIENT = 25 down , RNGFND1_GNDCLEAR sensor height above the ground when parked . What it gives you: height above terrain terrain following, TERRAIN_ and WP_RFND_USE before 4.7 — WPNAV_RFND_USE , precision landing LAND_ALT_LOW , and an EKF altitude source near the ground EK3_SRC1_POSZ = 2 , EK3_RNG_USE_HGT — the percentage of max range up to which the EKF uses the rangefinder . Over tall grass/bushes the rangefinder gives you the “terrain,” not the ground — that's not a sensor error. Optical flow A downward-facing camera PX4Flow, Cheerson CX-OF, Matek 3901-L0X, HereFlow measures the angular rate of image motion rad/s . To get linear velocity you need: height above the surface a rangefinder! and the aircraft's angular rate gyro to subtract rotation. v = flow − ω × h. That's why flow without a rangefinder only gives rough stabilization. Limitations: texture a plain floor, water, snow — doesn't work , lighting night without illumination , height 0.3–10 m typical , speed motion blur . Calibrate FLOW_FXSCALER/FYSCALER in flight: the test is rocking over a textured surface and comparing OF.flowX with OF.bodyX ArduPilot log OF . Connection: FLOW_TYPE 1 PX4Flow I2C, 5 MAVLink, 6 DroneCAN, 7 MSP , orientation FLOW_ORIENT_YAW , offset relative to the IMU FLOW_POS_ . EKF source: EK3_SRC1_VELXY = 5 . Building a source set EKF3 has three source sets EK3_SRC1_ , SRC2 , SRC3 , switched with a switch RCx_OPTION = 90 or a Lua script. Each one has: POSXY , VELXY , POSZ , VELZ , YAW . {{diagram:ekf-source-tree Choosing EKF3 sources for the scenario: with GPS, with flow and a rangefinder, with external navigation.}} Scenario POSXY VELXY POSZ YAW Comment --- --- --- --- --- --- Open field, GPS 3 GPS 3 GPS 1 Baro 1 Compass standard Indoors, textured floor 0 None 5 OptFlow 2 RangeFinder 1 Compass / 0 no GPS; the compass often lies indoors — then yaw 0 and heading is held by the gyro only drift Forest, GPS present but jumping 3 GPS 5 OptFlow 2 RangeFinder low / 1 Baro 1 Compass flow smooths out GPS jumps Precision landing 3 GPS 3 GPS 2 RangeFinder 1 rangefinder near the ground EK3_SRC_OPTIONS = 1 — fuse all velocities use velocities from all configured sources at once . Flying without GPS and without flow is Stabilize/AltHold only; Loiter/Auto are unavailable preflight check “PreArm: Need Position Estimate” . INAV Optical flow opflow_hardware , scale opflow_scale and the rangefinder rangefinder_hardware feed into the INAV position estimator via the weights inav_w_xy_flow_p / inav_w_xy_flow_v the flow weight in position and velocity ; for indoor flights on flow the documentation recommends inav_allow_dead_reckoning = ON “may be useful for indoor navigation with OPFLOW” . Position hold without GPS is POSHOLD mode with flow and a rangefinder set up, over a textured surface. practice Step 1. Baro A 10-minute log on the ground after power-on: BARO.Alt — the drift from warm-up. Then a hover at 2 m over a flat pad: BARO.Alt against RFND.Dist — see the prop-wash effect on takeoff. Step 2. Rangefinder Connect it, set up RNGFND1_ , check in the GCS that the value when parked = GNDCLEAR . Flight: is RFND.Dist smooth, with no spikes over grass? Record it. Step 3. SITL without GPS ArduPilot SITL --add-param-file with: SIM_GPS1_ENABLE = 0 in older versions SIM_GPS_DISABLE = 1 , FLOW_TYPE = 10 SITL , RNGFND1_TYPE = 100 SITL , EK3_SRC1_POSXY = 0 , EK3_SRC1_VELXY = 5 , EK3_SRC1_POSZ = 2 , EK3_SRC1_YAW = 1 . Take off in Loiter, hold position for 60 s, then move with the sticks: record the position drift XKF1.PN/PE . Repeat with SRC1_POSZ = 1 — see the difference in altitude. Step 4. Bench/flight With real flow and a rangefinder: hold in Loiter without GPS over a textured floor at 1–1.5 m, with an observer and a net/tether. title: Navigation and link resilience to interference
summary: GNSS and the compass are the most vulnerable sensors on board: the satellite signal is weaker than thermal noise, and the Earth's magnetic field is weaker than the field of a power wire. Degradation can be accidental (construction sites, power lines, your own interference, multipath) or intentional;
headings: Types of degradation and their log signature What the firmware does on its own Designing for resilience Frequency and power planning at the site What's out of scope Step 1. Signatures in SITL Step 2. Configure the reaction Step 3. Field test (civilian) Step 4. Site frequency plan
text: summary GNSS and the compass are the most vulnerable sensors on board: the satellite signal is weaker than thermal noise, and the Earth's magnetic field is weaker than the field of a power wire. Degradation can be accidental construction sites, power lines, your own interference, multipath or intentional; the engineer designs the vehicle so that it notices the degradation and reacts to it safely . This module is civilian: how to recognize the problem from logs NSats, HDOP, innovations, GPS glitch, heading jumps , how to set up backup EKF sources and the behavior on GPS/compass loss, how to plan RC/video frequencies and power at a site with other people's transmitters, and how to test every scenario in SITL. theory Types of degradation and their log signature What's happening GPS.NSats GPS.HDop / GPA.HAcc XKF4.SP/SV Other signs --- --- --- --- --- Partial sky obstruction wall, forest drops gradually grows creep up position “wanders” by meters Multipath normal HAcc jumps SP spikes 1 position jumps, velocity normal Wideband interference your own electronics, someone else's transmitter drops sharply to 0–3 HAcc → hundreds of m SV, SP grow, then GPS glitch coincides with a device switching on/approaching a site; satellite C/N0 drops GRAW /u-center Spoofing “good” fix “excellent” accuracy SP/SV grow: the model disagrees with the measurement position jump with normal satellites; GPS velocity contradicts accel; disagreement with baro/flow Magnetic anomaly/compass interference — — SM 1, yaw reset in XKF messages heading jumps, “toilet bowling,” “Compass variance” The main tool is source disagreement : the EKF compares every measurement with the prediction from the inertial sensors. The inertial sensors aren't affected by external interference — that's why innovations grow first. The second tool is signal quality at the receiver itself: the number of satellites and the signal-to-noise ratio per-satellite C/N0 in u-center; in ArduPilot — raw GPS data logging, GPS_RAW_DATA . The combination “satellites normal, innovations growing” suggests spoofing or a wrong model; “no satellites” suggests jamming or an obstructed sky. What the firmware does on its own - ArduPilot : GPS glitch protection innovation gates; when the radial disagreement exceeds EK3_GLITCH_RAD , 25 m by default, position and velocity are reset to GPS , lane switching between EKF cores, EKF failsafe FS_EKF_ACTION : 0 message only, 1 Land if the mode requires position, 2 AltHold if it requires position, 3 Land from any mode; threshold FS_EKF_THRESH , GPS failsafe via the EKF on loss of position in a mode that requires it — switch to Land/AltHold , yaw source fallback EK3_SRC1_YAW = 3 GPS with compass fallback; GSF yaw estimation from motion — EK3_SRC1_YAW = 8 or automatically with COMPASS_USE = 0 . Dead reckoning from inertial sensors and wind gives tens of seconds of acceptable accuracy, not minutes. - PX4 : EKF2_GPS_CHECK GPS quality check bitmask , accuracy threshold COM_POS_FS_EPH ; loss-of-position failsafe COM_POSCTL_NAVL 0 — RC available: switch to Altitude/Stabilized; 1 — no RC: Descend or flight termination ; u-blox receivers have built-in jamming detection a sensitivity parameter in the GPS driver , and the state is published in the sensor_gps message. - INAV : if there is no position for longer than ~2 s in RTH/WP — Emergency Landing descent in ANGLE at failsafe_throttle , motors cut after failsafe_off_delay ; failsafe_procedure is the reaction to RC loss, not GPS loss; dead reckoning inav_allow_dead_reckoning , inav_allow_gps_fix_estimation estimation without a fix for a wing, based on airspeed + compass . Designing for resilience 1. Reduce your own interference see the EMI module : this accounts for 80% of real GPS problems. 2. Backup EKF sources : optical flow + rangefinder for low altitudes; baro as the POSZ backup; a second GPS with GPS_AUTO_SWITCH ; compass + GPS yaw + GSF. 3. A failsafe that fits the scenario : what to do on loss of position depends on the location. Over a field: AltHold and a manual landing. Over people: Land. Over water: continuing to shore on inertial navigation — don't count on it, it won't last. The decision is recorded in the engineering folder with its rationale. 4. GPS-independent modes are always available to the pilot : Stabilize/AltHold on a switch, and the pilot knows how to use them — this is practiced in training. 5. Geofence and altitude : when position degrades, the geofence is useless — account for this in the site risk assessment. Frequency and power planning at the site - A table of occupied video channels and RC bands the “Field Operations” module : a new participant adds themselves to it instead of switching on a transmitter at random. - RC: 2.4 GHz and 900 MHz degrade differently; 900 MHz handles range and obstacles better, 2.4 GHz is more crowded Wi-Fi, other radios . Two receivers on two bands give a backup link. - Power: the minimum that's sufficient per the link budget the “Link Budget” module — extra watts jam your neighbors and heat the VTX; on the ground — minimum power pit mode . - Telemetry: a separate channel 900 MHz/4G/LTE for monitoring status if RC and video are lost. - Legality of bands and power — the “Regulations” module. What's out of scope Methods of creating interference, countering specific jamming systems, bypassing restrictions — outside this course and illegal in most jurisdictions. The course teaches you to detect and safely end the flight , not to “punch through.” {{diagram:degradation-signatures How to tell types of navigation degradation apart from the log: satellites and accuracy, EKF innovations, compass.}} practice Step 1. Signatures in SITL ArduPilot SITL, Loiter at 20 m: - GPS loss : SIM_GPS1_ENABLE = 0 older versions: SIM_GPS_DISABLE = 1 for 30 s → what the vehicle does, when the EKF failsafe triggers, how XKF4.SP , XKF1.PN/PE and the messages in MSG behave. - GNSS noise : SIM_GPS1_NOISE older: SIM_GPS_NOISE = 5 m → innovations, Loiter drift. - Posi

text: summary ArduPilot is an autopilot, not just a stabilizer. If Betaflight makes a quadcopter obedient under the sticks, ArduPilot knows where it is, where it is going and what to do without a pilot. This module explains how thinking in ArduPilot differs from Betaflight: parameters instead of CLI diffs, flight modes as levels of autonomy, the ground control station, pre-arm checks and hardware requirements. After it, the whole “Autonomy” track opens up. theory Versions and parameter names The course is written for ArduPilot 4.5 and newer. In Copter 4.7 stable since July 2026 some parameters were renamed and moved to SI units: ARMING_CHECK → ARMING_SKIPCHK the meaning is inverted: a list of checks to skip , 0 — all enabled , WPNAV_ → WP_ m, m/s , RTL_ALT → RTL_ALT_M m , ATC_ACCEL_ _MAX → ATC_ACC_ _MAX °/s² , PSC_ACCZ_ → PSC_D_ACC_ . In Plane since 4.5 ARSPD_FBW_MIN/MAX → AIRSPEED_MIN/MAX . The modules give the new name with the old one in parentheses; when you update the firmware, old values are converted automatically, but you have to fix your own scripts and parameter files by hand. One codebase — many vehicles ArduPilot is shared code with separate firmware per vehicle type: Copter multirotors and helicopters , Plane planes, wings and QuadPlane VTOL , Rover, Sub. The frame type within a firmware is set with parameters: for Copter that is FRAME_CLASS 1 — Quad, 2 — Hexa, 3 — Octa, 4 — OctaQuad, 7 — Tri… and FRAME_TYPE 0 — Plus, 1 — X, 2 — V, 3 — H… . {{diagram:ardupilot-fast-loop How the ArduCopter loop works: sensors → EKF → mode controllers → rate controller → motors.}} Parameters All configuration is parameters there are more than a thousand of them . The key difference from Betaflight: a parameter change is written immediately, there is no save command. Some parameters require a reboot frame type, protocols, enabling subsystems . The workflow: 1. Save the full parameter list to a file .param before making changes. 2. Change one logical block at a time. 3. Compare the parameter files before and after — like diff all in Betaflight. Flight modes Modes are levels of autonomy. For Copter: - STABILIZE — self-leveling, manual throttle. The basic mode, works without GPS. - ALT_HOLD — plus altitude hold from the barometer. - LOITER — plus position hold, needs GPS. - AUTO — mission execution. - GUIDED — commands from the ground control station or a script the basis for companion computers . - RTL and LAND — return to home and landing. The rule: you choose the mode by which sensors you trust. No GPS — no LOITER, RTL or AUTO. Ground control station and MAVLink You set up ArduPilot through a ground control station GCS : Mission Planner, QGroundControl or the console-based MAVProxy. They all talk to the flight controller over MAVLink — the same protocol your companion computer will use later. Pre-arm checks ArduPilot will not arm while something is wrong: the accelerometer or compass is not calibrated, there is no link, the EKF is bad, parameters are wrong. A PreArm: ... message in the GCS is a hint, not a nuisance. Disabling checks so that it “just flies” is the classic road to a crash. Hardware requirements ArduPilot is noticeably heavier than Betaflight. On F4 controllers some features are not available: for example, Lua scripts need at least 2 MB of flash and do not work on F4. For complex platforms people use H7. What changes for a Betaflight pilot - Parameter files, not diffs. - Not “flash it and fly”, but calibrations accelerometer, compass, radio, ESC and pre-arm. - DataFlash logs .bin are recorded almost always and contain everything: from vibration to EKF decisions. - Tuning more often starts with AUTOTUNE rather than manual PID. Copter modes by number FLTMODE1..6 , values from Parameters.cpp 0 Stabilize, 1 Acro, 2 AltHold, 3 Auto, 4 Guided, 5 Loiter, 6 RTL, 7 Circle, 9 Land, 11 Drift, 13 Sport, 14 Flip, 15 AutoTune, 16 PosHold, 17 Brake, 18 Throw, 20 Guided_NoGPS, 21 Smart_RTL, 22 FlowHold, 23 Follow, 24 ZigZag, 25 SystemID, 27 Auto RTL, 28 Turtle. Six positions of the FLTMODE_CH channel PWM boundaries 1230/1360/1490/1620/1749 + any modes on RCx_OPTION . Groups by sensor requirements: without position — Stabilize, Acro, AltHold baro , Land partially , FlowHold flow ; with position — Loiter, PosHold, Auto, Guided, RTL, Smart_RTL, Circle, Follow, ZigZag, Brake. The first flight of any build is Stabilize → AltHold → Loiter, in that order. First setup order Mission Planner / QGC 1. Firmware for the board type hwdef , choosing the frame class/type FRAME_CLASS , FRAME_TYPE . 2. Calibrations: accelerometer 6 positions , level, compass in the field , radio RC1..4_MIN/MAX/TRIM , ESC MOT_PWM_TYPE DShot — no calibration needed , voltage/current sensor BATT_MONITOR , BATT_VOLT_MULT , BATT_AMP_PERVLT against a wattmeter . 3. Modes on switches, RCx_OPTION ARM/DISARM, Motor E-Stop, EKF source set… . 4. Failsafe the “Fault Tolerance” module , geofence, RTL_ALT_M . 5. Starting tuning parameters by prop size the “ArduPilot Tuning” module : INS_GYRO_FILTER , ATC_RAT_ _FLT , MOT_THST_EXPO , ATC_INPUT_TC , PSC_D_ACC_ before 4.7 — PSC_ACCZ_ . 6. Logs LOG_BITMASK , LOG_DISARMED for ground measurements. 7. Motor test Mission Planner → Optional Hardware → Motor Test with props off: order and direction per the frame type diagram. text: summary SITL Software In The Loop is the real ArduPilot firmware running on a computer instead of a flight controller, with a physics simulator instead of the real world. Here you can crash a hundred octocopters for free: mix up parameters, kill GPS in flight, drop a motor. This module shows how to bring up SITL, connect a ground station, control the drone with a Python script, and organize the project so that routes and scenarios live separately. theory How SITL works The firmware is built for Linux and exchanges “sensor readings” and “motor commands” with the physics simulator. Everything else is real: the same parameters, modes, EKF, failsafes, logs. So everything you debugged in SITL carries over to hardware almost unchanged. Almost — because in simulation the vibrations are perfect, the link is perfect and GPS is honest, unless you break them yourself. sim_vehicle.py and MAVProxy The sim_vehicle.py script builds the firmware, starts it and starts the MAVProxy console ground station. Key flags: - -v ArduCopter or -v ArduPlane — vehicle type; - -f octa-quad , -f quad , -f quadplane — frame model in the simulator; - --console --map — console and map windows; - -w — wipe parameters to defaults useful when experiments went sideways . A ground station QGroundControl, Mission Planner connects to the MAVProxy output over UDP — usually it finds it on its own. Scenario vs. route The main architectural decision in the course project: the route and the scenario live separately. - Route — only a sequence of points in a single format. The first point is the start, the last one is the finish. - Scenario — only commands: takeoff, “fly route X”, landing, motor failure at the third waypoint. There are no coordinates in a scenario. That way one route runs under different scenarios, and one scenario runs over different routes. It's the same idea as separating data and logic in any decent code. What SITL can do besides “just fly” - Frame models -f : quad, hexa, octa, octa-quad X8 , y6, tri, heli, plane, quadplane, quadplane-tilttri/quadplane-tilt tiltrotors , rover, boat, sub — each has its own physics in libraries/SITL/SIM_ .cpp ; default parameters for a model are in Tools/autotest/default_params/ .parm . - Failures and environment via SIM_ : wind SIM_WIND_SPD/DIR/TURB , motor failure SIM_ENGINE_FAIL + SIM_ENGINE_MUL , GPS disable, noise, glitch, lag , compass offset , baro drift/glitch , vibration SIM_VIB_ , RC loss SIM_RC_FAIL , battery voltage SIM_BATT_VOLTAGE , rangefinder and optical flow RNGFND1_TYPE = 100 , FLOW_TYPE = 10 . This is the foundation of the “Fault tolerance” and “Navigation resilience” modules. - Time acceleration --speedup 10 for long missions; --add-param-file for your own parameters; --out=udp:IP:14550 for an external GCS; --no-mavproxy for scripts. - External physics engines : Gazebo -f gazebo-iris , RealFlight, X-Plane, JSBSim wing , Webots — when you need aerodynamics/visualization; for failsafe and mission logic the built-in physics is enough. - Lua and companion : scripts SCR_ENABLE = 1 , a scripts/ folder next to where you launch and MAVLink clients tcp:127.0.0.1:5760 , the next ones — 5762/5763 work just like on hardware. SITL logs and reading them Logs are written to logs/ in the working folder .BIN and are read with the same tools as real ones mavexplorer.py , Mission Planner, pymavlink — the “Python for data” module . That is the whole point of SITL: practicing the analysis method before real flights. Worked example: testing a mission with a failure sim_vehicle.py -v ArduCopter -f hexa --console --map --speedup 5 ; load the mission wp load mission.txt , mode auto , arm throttle ; at the third waypoint param set SIM_ENGINE_FAIL 4 motor 3, bitmask , watch RCOU , altitude, yaw; set it back to 0 ; then param set SIM_RC_FAIL 1 in Loiter — check FS_THR_ENABLE . The result goes into the test log the “Fault tolerance” module : scenario, expectation, actual result, log. The scenario can be written as a pymavlink script — a template is in examples/sitl-pymavlink in the course repo. Where SITL lies No vibration or motor noise you can't test filters , perfect mechanics, ESCs without latency, GPS with a configured noise level, no compass interference except what is modeled. PID tuning parameters from SITL do not carry over to a real vehicle; what carries over is logic, missions, scripts, failsafes and analysis skills. {{diagram:sitl-arch SITL: the same ArduCopter code gets sensor data from a physics model; MAVProxy distributes MAVLink to the GCS and scripts, logs are written just like in flight.}} practice Step 1. Installation Ubuntu git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot.git cd ardupilot Tools/environment_install/install-prereqs-ubuntu.sh -y . ~/.profile Step 2. First run sim_vehicle.py -v ArduCopter -f octa-quad --console --map -w In the MAVProxy console: mode guided arm throttle takeoff 10 The drone will take off to 10 m. mode rtl brings it back home. Step 3. Control from a script pymavlink SITL opens additional TCP ports for external clients. An example of a takeoff from a script: python from pymavlink import mavutil master = mavutil.mavlink_connection "tcp:127.0.0.1:5762" master.wait_heartbeat print "connected to system", master.target_system master.set_mode master.mode_mapping "GUIDED" master.arducopter_arm master.motors_armed_wait master.mav.command_long_send master.target_system, master.target_component, mavutil.mavlink.MAV_CMD_NAV_TAKEOFF, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 10, param7 = altitude, m while True: msg = master.recv_match type="GLOBAL_POSITION_INT", blocking=True alt = msg.relative_alt / 1000 print f"alt {alt:.1f} m" if alt 9.5: break Step 4. title: Simulation in Gazebo: worlds, sensors, a camera in ROS 2 and scenario tests
summary: SITL без внешнего симулятора считает физику простой встроенной моделью и не знает, что такое дерево, стена или изображение с камеры. Для зрения, обхода препятствий, точной посадки и подвесов нужен мир: Gazebo даёт физику, освещение, камеры, лидары и дальномеры, а автопилот работает с ним как с насто
headings: Какой Gazebo Как автопилот говорит с миром Мир на SDF Датчики и мост в ROS 2 Скорость и ресурсы HITL и SITL Сценарные тесты Шаг 1. Iris в Gazebo Шаг 2. Свой мир со столбом Шаг 3. Камера в ROS 2 Шаг 4. Сценарный тест
text: summary SITL без внешнего симулятора считает физику простой встроенной моделью и не знает, что такое дерево, стена или изображение с камеры. Для зрения, обхода препятствий, точной посадки и подвесов нужен мир: Gazebo даёт физику, освещение, камеры, лидары и дальномеры, а автопилот работает с ним как с настоящим аппаратом. Модуль разбирает связку ArduPilot SITL и PX4 SITL с Gazebo новым, gz , устройство мира на SDF, добавление препятствия и камеры, мост изображений в ROS 2, сценарные тесты без графики для CI и что такое HITL и чем он отличается от SITL. theory Какой Gazebo - Gazebo gz — новая линейка бывший Ignition . Для ROS 2 Jazzy парная LTS-версия — Gazebo Harmonic ; её же рекомендует плагин ArduPilot. - Gazebo Classic gazebo11 закончил поддержку в январе 2025 — старые инструкции с gazebo --verbose и .world для Classic не переносить. - Пара «ROS 2 — Gazebo» фиксирована: смешивать версии мимо рекомендованных пар — источник трудноуловимых проблем со сборкой мостов. Как автопилот говорит с миром - ArduPilot : плагин ardupilot_gazebo система ArduPilotPlugin в модели . Gazebo считает физику и датчики, плагин отправляет состояние в SITL и получает от него команды моторам/сервам; обмен — JSON по UDP, в режиме lockstep симуляция ждёт автопилот, время согласовано . Запуск: в одном терминале gz sim -v4 -r iris_runway.sdf , в другом sim_vehicle.py -v ArduCopter -f gazebo-iris --model JSON --map --console . Имя фрейма должно содержать gazebo- , модель — JSON . - PX4 : Gazebo встроен в сборку SITL: make px4_sitl gz_x500 ; варианты моделей с датчиками например gz_x500_depth , gz_x500_mono_cam и самолёты/VTOL; мир выбирается переменной PX4_GZ_WORLD . - Переменные окружения: GZ_SIM_SYSTEM_PLUGIN_PATH — где искать плагины сборка ardupilot_gazebo , GZ_SIM_RESOURCE_PATH — модели и миры. Мир на SDF Мир — XML-файл SDF: физика шаг, например 1 мс , освещение, земля, модели. Модель — звенья link с геометрией столкновений collision и видимой visual , массой и инерцией, суставы joint , датчики sensor и системы-плагины. Препятствие — статическая модель: xml <model name="pole" <static true</static <pose 10 0 5 0 0 0</pose <link name="link" <collision name="collision" <geometry <cylinder <radius 0.3</radius <length 10</length </cylinder </geometry </collision <visual name="visual" <geometry <cylinder <radius 0.3</radius <length 10</length </cylinder </geometry </visual </link </model Столб 10 м высотой, в 10 м к востоку от начала координат мира ENU: x — восток, y — север, z — вверх . Датчики и мост в ROS 2 - Камеры, камеры глубины, лидары gpu_lidar , IMU — элементы sensor в модели; публикуют в шину Gazebo gz-transport , список — gz topic -l . - ros_gz_bridge переносит топики между Gazebo и ROS 2: ros2 run ros_gz_bridge parameter_bridge /camera@sensor_msgs/msg/Image@gz.msgs.Image — имя топика, тип ROS 2, тип Gazebo; @ — в обе стороны, — из Gazebo в ROS, — из ROS в Gazebo. - Отдельный плагин GstCameraPlugin из ardupilot_gazebo отдаёт видео с камеры по GStreamer H.264, UDP 5600 — как настоящая камера на companion; поток включается сообщением в топик .../enable_streaming . Пример мира с подвесом и камерой — gimbal.sdf ; подвес Iris в iris_runway.sdf SITL с gazebo-iris-gimbal.parm управляется каналами RC6–RC8. - Реализм: идеальная камера без шума и размытия обманывает — алгоритмы зрения стоит проверять с шумом, сменой освещения и размытием движения параметры шума в описании датчика . Скорость и ресурсы - Real-time factor RTF — отношение скорости симуляции к реальному времени; с камерами и лидарами на слабой машине падает ниже 1. Lockstep сохраняет корректность, но тест длится дольше. - Рендеринг нужен только датчикам изображения; для тестов логики без камер — сервер без графики gz sim -s -r мир.sdf , для камер на машине без экрана — режим --headless-rendering . HITL и SITL - SITL — прошивка собрана под компьютер, всё виртуальное. - HITL hardware in the loop — настоящий полётник со своей прошивкой, датчики подменяются данными симулятора по USB/MAVLink, моторы не крутятся. Проверяет реальное железо: тайминги, загрузку процессора, драйверы, что SITL скрывает. Поддержка и способ настройки отличаются у PX4 и ArduPilot и между версиями — по документации своей версии. Сценарные тесты Сценарий — воспроизводимый полёт с проверкой результата: «взлёт на 10 м, облёт столба, посадка; не ближе 2 м к столбу, высота в допуске». Запуск без графики, проверка через MAVLink и лог, результат — pass/fail для CI модуль «Конфигурации в CI» . Один сценарий на каждую функцию безопасности failsafe, геозона, RTL ловит регрессии при обновлении прошивки и параметров раньше поля. {{diagram:gazebo-sitl Gazebo считает физику и датчики, плагин обменивается с SITL по JSON в lockstep; изображения идут в ROS 2 через ros_gz_bridge, наземка и тесты подключаются к SITL по MAVLink.}} practice Шаг 1. Iris в Gazebo Установить Gazebo Harmonic и собрать ardupilot_gazebo по README зависимости, cmake , make , выставить GZ_SIM_SYSTEM_PLUGIN_PATH и GZ_SIM_RESOURCE_PATH . Запустить iris_runway.sdf и SITL с -f gazebo-iris --model JSON . Взлёт в GUIDED на 10 м из MAVProxy. Записать RTF при висении. Шаг 2. Свой мир со столбом Скопировать iris_runway.sdf в свой мир, добавить столб из теории. Миссия: взлёт, точка в 20 м к востоку на высоте 5 м, возврат. Что происходит с аппаратом без обхода препятствий? Перенести точку так, чтобы маршрут проходил в 3 м от столба. Шаг 3. Камера в ROS 2 Запустить мир с камерой gimbal.sdf или модель с камерой , найти топик изображения gz topic -l , поднять мост в ROS 2 и проверить ros2 topic hz и rqt_image_view или ros2 run image_tools showimage . Записать частоту кадров и разрешение. Шаг 4. Сценарный тест pytest-сценарий против SITL Gazebo без графики: gz sim -s -r мир.sdf : python import time from pymavlink import mavutil def test_takeoff_hold_land : m = mavutil.mavlink_connection "udpin:0.0.0.0:14550" m.wait_heartbeat timeout=30 m.set_mode "GUIDED" deadline = time.time + 60 while not m.motors_armed : pre-arm checks pass once EKF and GPS a

summary: A mission in ArduPilot is a list of commands the flight controller executes on its own in AUTO mode: take off, fly through waypoints, take a picture, come back. A mission in SITL via the GCS Step 2. The same mission from code Step 3. Scenarios on top of a route
text: summary A mission in ArduPilot is a list of commands the flight controller executes on its own in AUTO mode: take off, fly through waypoints, take a picture, come back. This module explains what a mission is made of, how navigation commands differ from DO and CONDITION commands, how altitude is calculated, where home is, and what happens when the link is lost mid-route. Practice is in SITL, following the “route separately, scenario separately” pattern. theory Three types of commands - NAV — where to fly. NAV_TAKEOFF 22 , NAV_WAYPOINT 16 , NAV_LOITER_TIME 19 , NAV_RETURN_TO_LAUNCH 20 , NAV_LAND 21 . The mission goes from one NAV command to the next. - DO — what to do along the way without changing the route: DO_CHANGE_SPEED 178 , DO_SET_SERVO 183 , DO_SET_CAM_TRIGG_DIST 206 , DO_JUMP 177 for loops. - CONDITION — wait for a condition before the next DO command: CONDITION_DELAY 112 , CONDITION_DISTANCE . The numbers in parentheses are MAV_CMD codes: that's how the commands look in a mission file and in MAVLink. Altitude Every waypoint has a reference frame. For missions you almost always use altitude relative to home MAV_FRAME_GLOBAL_RELATIVE_ALT , code 3 : “100 m” means 100 m above the arming point. Absolute altitude above sea level MAV_FRAME_GLOBAL , 0 is rarely needed and easily leads to an error of hundreds of meters. Altitude above terrain requires terrain data. Home For Copter, the home point is where the aircraft armed. RTL returns there, not to where the pilot is standing. If you took off from the roof of a car and then drove somewhere else — home stayed at the old spot. In the GCS you can reset home before takeoff. Starting and resuming A Copter mission usually starts with NAV_TAKEOFF . Switching to AUTO on the ground with the aircraft armed starts the takeoff once the pilot raises the throttle or immediately, if bit 1 “Allow Takeoff Without Raising Throttle” is set in AUTO_OPTIONS ; in SITL — rc 3 1500 . By default, when you re-enter AUTO the mission continues from the current command; the MIS_RESTART parameter makes it start from the first one. Failsafe during a mission Loss of the radio link during AUTO behaves per FS_THR_ENABLE RTL, Land, SmartRTL… , and continuing the mission is enabled by bit 0 of FS_OPTIONS . For autonomous beyond-visual-line-of-sight flights this decision is made before takeoff, not after the fact. GCS loss is a separate parameter, FS_GCS_ENABLE . The battery failsafe BATT_FS_LOW_ACT , BATT_FS_CRT_ACT overrides the mission. Mission file GCSs save the mission to a text file in the QGC WPL 110 format: one line per command — index, current flag, frame, command code, four parameters, latitude, longitude, altitude, autocontinue flag. Such a file is convenient to keep in git next to the parameters. Commands worth knowing by heart NAV: NAV_WAYPOINT p1 — delay at the waypoint, s , NAV_TAKEOFF alt , NAV_LAND , NAV_RETURN_TO_LAUNCH , NAV_LOITER_TIME/TURNS/UNLIM , NAV_SPLINE_WAYPOINT spline , NAV_DELAY ; DO: DO_SET_SERVO , DO_SET_RELAY , DO_DIGICAM_CONTROL , DO_SET_CAM_TRIGG_DIST a shot every N m — the basis of photogrammetry , DO_CHANGE_SPEED , DO_SET_ROI point the gimbal/nose , DO_JUMP a loop, with a counter , DO_LAND_START the entry point of the landing sequence for a failsafe , DO_SET_HOME ; CONDITION: CONDITION_DELAY , CONDITION_DISTANCE , CONDITION_YAW . Execution parameters: WP_SPD m/s horizontal , WP_SPD_UP/DN , WP_RADIUS_M acceptance radius , WP_ACC before 4.7 — WPNAV_SPEED in cm/s, WPNAV_SPEED_UP/DN , WPNAV_RADIUS , WPNAV_ACCEL , WP_YAW_BEHAVIOR nose along the course or not , MIS_RESTART 0 — resume from the last command when entering Auto, 1 — from the start , MIS_OPTIONS bit 0 — clear the mission on reboot; bit 1 — use distance to landing in the battery failsafe Plane only ; bit 2 — continue after landing , RTL_ for the end of the mission. Altitudes: three frames and one mistake Relative above home, MAV_FRAME_GLOBAL_RELATIVE_ALT , the default , absolute above sea level — wrong if you take off somewhere else , terrain above ground from SRTM data via the GCS or from a rangefinder, TERRAIN_ENABLE , the “Terrain” frame on waypoints and WP_RFND_USE / RTL_ALT_TYPE . The classic crash: a mission with absolute altitudes, made for a different site 300 m higher — the aircraft tries to dive into the ground or climb into the sky. The rule: relative altitudes, and check the altitude-above-terrain profile in the GCS. Worked example: surveying a 300×200 m area Mission Planner → Survey Grid : camera sensor, focal length , altitude 80 m, overlap 75/65% → the planner calculates the spacing between survey lines and DO_SET_CAM_TRIGG_DIST itself; speed 8 m/s based on camera exposure: motion blur ≤ 1 px → v·t_exp ≤ GSD ; NAV_TAKEOFF 80, survey lines, DO_SET_CAM_TRIGG_DIST 0 at the end, NAV_RETURN_TO_LAUNCH . Checks: the altitude profile, mission time vs. battery capacity BATT_LOW_MAH with margin for RTL + capacity margin for the return , a geofence around the area. A run in SITL with the same mission file is mandatory. {{diagram:mission-alt-frames Choosing the altitude frame in a mission: Relative for flat ground, Terrain for varying terrain, Absolute when altitude above sea level is given.}} practice Step 1. A mission in SITL via the GCS 1. Start SITL: sim_vehicle.py -v ArduCopter --console --map . 2. In Mission Planner Plan or QGC Plan , set TAKEOFF 20 m, three waypoints, RTL. 3. Write the mission to the aircraft, save the .waypoints file. 4. Arm, AUTO mode, watch. Then try switching to LOITER mid-route and back to AUTO. Step 2. The same mission from code The route is data, the scenario is commands. An example of uploading a route via pymavlink: python from pymavlink import mavutil ROUTE = lat, lon, alt_m — data only, no commands here -35.3630, 149.1652, 30 , -35.3625, 149.1660, 30 , -35.3632, 149.1668, 30 , m = mavutil.mavlink_connection "tcp:127.0.0.1:5762" m.wait_heartbeat FRAME = mavutil.mavlink.MAV_FRAME_GLOBAL_RELATIVE_ALT_INT 6 def item seq, cmd, lat=0, lon=0, alt=0, p1

title: Guidance and trajectories: pure pursuit, L1, S-curves, minimum snap
summary: Регуляторы курса держат угол, скорость и позицию. Но кто решает, *какую* позицию держать в каждый момент, чтобы аппарат прошёл по линии миссии, плавно повернул и не дёрнулся? Это наведение и генерация траекторий. Модуль разбирает слои от миссии до регулятора, закон pure pursuit и его родственника L1
headings: Слои: от точек к моторам Pure pursuit L1 в ArduPlane и NPFG в PX4 Профили скорости: трапеция и S-кривая Minimum snap для квадрокоптера Feedforward: не только позиция Шаг 1. Pure pursuit в симуляции Шаг 2. L1 своего самолёта Шаг 3. Трапеция и S-кривая Шаг 4. SITL: рывок и скругление
text: summary Регуляторы курса держат угол, скорость и позицию. Но кто решает, какую позицию держать в каждый момент, чтобы аппарат прошёл по линии миссии, плавно повернул и не дёрнулся? Это наведение и генерация траекторий. Модуль разбирает слои от миссии до регулятора, закон pure pursuit и его родственника L1 в ArduPlane с формулой дальности упреждения через NAVL1_PERIOD , профили скорости — трапецию и S-кривую с ограничением рывка, которой ArduCopter ведёт по точкам, — и minimum snap для квадрокоптера с объяснением, почему именно «snap». Код симуляции воспроизводит графики модуля; лабораторная — подобрать упреждение по перелёту и времени выхода на линию. theory Слои: от точек к моторам 1. Миссия — список точек и действий модуль «Миссии» . 2. Путь — геометрия между точками: отрезки, дуги поворота, сплайны NAV_SPLINE_WAYPOINT . 3. Траектория — путь с временем: где аппарат должен быть в момент t, с какой скоростью и ускорением, в пределах ограничений скорости, ускорения и рывка. 4. Наведение / слежение — превращает отклонение от пути или траектории в команду ускорение, крен, скорость для регулятора позиции. Следование пути path following не заботится о времени — главное быть на линии. Слежение за траекторией trajectory tracking требует быть в точке вовремя — для строя, синхронной съёмки, совместных манёвров. Pure pursuit Аппарат «гонится» за точкой на пути, лежащей на расстоянии L впереди дальность упреждения . Если α — угол между вектором скорости и направлением на эту точку, то кривизна, выводящая на неё по дуге, κ = 2·sin α / L, а боковое ускорение a = V²·κ = 2·V²·sin α / L. - Малое L — резкий выход на линию, перелёт и чувствительность к шуму позиции. - Большое L — плавно, но медленно, и углы маршрута «срезаются». - При 20 м сбоку и 10 м/с симуляция ниже : L = 8 м — перелёт ~3 м; L = 20 м — перелёт ~1 м, в коридоре ±1 м через 35 м пути; L = 45 м — в коридоре только через ~90 м. {{diagram:chart-pure-pursuit Pure pursuit с 20 м сбоку при 10 м/с: малое упреждение даёт перелёт, большое — долгий выход на линию.}} L1 в ArduPlane и NPFG в PX4 L1 — тот же закон бокового ускорения в ArduPilot с коэффициентом 4ζ² вместо 2: a = 4ζ²·V²·sin η / L1, при ζ = 0.707 — ровно pure pursuit , но дальность упреждения растёт со скоростью, чтобы динамика выхода на линию не зависела от скорости: L1 = 1/π ·ζ·T·V, где T = NAVL1_PERIOD , ζ = NAVL1_DAMPING , V — путевая скорость. - Пример: V = 18 м/с, T = 17 с, ζ = 0.75 → L1 ≈ 0.318·0.75·17·18 ≈ 73 м. - Уменьшение NAVL1_PERIOD укорачивает L1 — резче повороты, риск вилять настройка — в модуле «Тюнинг ArduPlane» . - Боковое ускорение превращается в крен: tan φ = a / g, с ограничением ROLL_LIMIT_DEG . В PX4 для самолётов наведение ведёт NPFG nonlinear path following guidance : тот же принцип упреждения плюс явная обработка ветра, сравнимого со скоростью самолёта, — когда удержать линию нельзя, NPFG выбирает выполнимое направление, а не «сдувается» вбок. Параметры периода и демпфирования NPFG_PERIOD , NPFG_DAMPING — по смыслу как у L1. Профили скорости: трапеция и S-кривая - Трапеция : разгон с постоянным ускорением, крейсер, торможение. Ускорение меняется скачком — рывок производная ускорения бесконечен. Для коптера скачок ускорения = скачок наклона: дёрганье, раскачка груза и камеры, перерегулирование. - S-кривая jerk-limited : ускорение нарастает с ограниченным рывком. Перемещение на 50 м при v ≤ 10 м/с, a ≤ 5 м/с², рывок ≤ 10 м/с³: трапеция — 7.0 с, S-кривая — 7.5 с +0.5 с за время нарастания ускорения , но без скачков. - ArduCopter с 4.1 строит путь по точкам S-кривыми: скорость, ускорение и рывок задаются параметрами навигации WPNAV_SPEED , см/с; WPNAV_ACCEL , см/с²; WPNAV_JERK , м/с³; в Copter 4.7 — WP_SPD , м/с; WP_ACC , м/с²; WP_JERK , м/с³ , углы маршрута скругляются с радиусом WPNAV_RADIUS 4.7 — WP_RADIUS_M . {{diagram:chart-scurve Ускорение при перемещении на 50 м: трапеция переключает ускорение скачком, S-кривая — с ограниченным рывком, ценой 0.5 с.}} Minimum snap для квадрокоптера Квадрокоптер — дифференциально плоская система: зная траекторию позиции и курса, можно вычислить всё остальное. Тяга определяется ускорением, угловая скорость корпуса — рывком третьей производной позиции , а моменты моторов — snap четвёртой производной . Поэтому траектория с минимальным интегралом квадрата snap даёт самые гладкие команды моторам. На практике: между точками — полиномы 7-го порядка по каждой оси, непрерывные до snap в стыках, коэффициенты — из задачи квадратичной оптимизации Mellinger, Kumar, 2011 . Такие траектории строят на companion и отправляют автопилоту как цели позиции вместе со скоростью и ускорением feedforward , иначе регулятор позиции отстаёт. Feedforward: не только позиция Если companion шлёт только позицию, регулятор узнаёт, что надо разгоняться, когда ошибка уже есть, — аппарат отстаёт на поворотах. SET_POSITION_TARGET_LOCAL_NED позволяет передать позицию, скорость и ускорение одновременно маска type_mask : регулятор позиции догоняет только остаток ошибки. practice Шаг 1. Pure pursuit в симуляции Скрипт воспроизводит график модуля и считает перелёт и расстояние до входа в коридор ±1 м: python import math def pursuit L, y0=20.0, V=10.0, a_max=8.0, T=15.0, dt=0.02 : """Kinematic vehicle, path = the x axis. Returns overshoot m and distance to settle within 1 m.""" x, y, psi = 0.0, y0, 0.0 overshoot, settle_x = 0.0, None for _ in range int T / dt : dx = math.sqrt L L - y y if abs y < L else 0.0 lookahead point on the path alpha = math.atan2 -y, max dx, 0.5 - psi alpha = math.atan2 math.sin alpha , math.cos alpha a = max -a_max, min a_max, 2 V V math.sin alpha / L a_lat = 2V² sin α / L psi += a / V dt x += V math.cos psi dt y += V math.sin psi dt overshoot = max overshoot, -y if abs y 1.0: settle_x = None elif settle_x is None: settle_x = x return overshoot, settle_x for L in 8, 20, 45 : o, s = pursuit L print f"L = {L:2d} м: перелёт {o:.1f} м, в коридоре ±1 м с {s:.0f} м" L = 8 м: перелёт 3.0 м, в коридоре ±1 м с 35 м L = 20 м: перелёт 1.0 м, в коридоре ±1 м
